title.zh: 卷五十七 列傳第四十七 沈約 范雲
title.en: Volume 57 Biographies 47: Shen Yue, Fan Yun
title.raw: 卷五十七 列傳第四十七 沈約 范雲 Volume 57 Biographies 47: Shen Yue, Fan Yun

sentences.zh: 列傳第四十七

translations.literal: Biographies 47
translations.idiomatic: the 47th year of Biographies

sentences.zh: 沈約范雲

translations.literal: Shen Yue and Fan Yun
translations.idiomatic: Shen Yue and Fan Yun

sentences.zh: 戎子酆字聖通，位零陵太守，致黃龍芝草之瑞。

translations.literal: Rongzi Feng, styled Shengtong, served as Governor of Lingling and brought about auspicious omens of yellow dragons and spirit fungus.
translations.idiomatic: A man of the Rong clan named Feng, styled Shengtong, held the post of governor of Lingling and was credited with prodigies of yellow dragons and miraculous fungus.

sentences.zh: 第二子仲高，安平相，少子景河間相，演之、慶之、曇慶、懷文其後也。

translations.literal: His second son Zhonggao was Chancellor of Anping; his youngest son Jing was Chancellor of Hejian. Yanzhi, Qingzhi, Tanqing, and Huaiwen were among their descendants.
translations.idiomatic: Zhonggao, the second son, became chancellor of Anping; Jing, the youngest, became chancellor of Hejian. Yanzhi, Qingzhi, Tanqing, and Huaiwen were descended from them.

sentences.zh: 仲高子鸞字建光，少有高名，州舉茂才，公府辟州別駕從事史。

translations.literal: Zhonggao's son Luan, styled Jianguang, enjoyed a lofty reputation from youth; the province nominated him as a Prominent Talent, and the chief regional office appointed him Attendant Secretary to the Provincial Governor.
translations.idiomatic: Luan, son of Zhonggao and styled Jianguang, was widely esteemed in his youth. The province recommended him as a promising talent, and the regional headquarters made him secretary to the governor.

sentences.zh: 時廣陵太守陸稠，鸞之舅也，以義烈政績顯名漢朝，復以女妻鸞，早卒。

translations.literal: At the time Lu Chou was Governor of Guangling and Luan's maternal uncle; renowned in the Han for righteous valor and administrative achievement, he also gave his daughter in marriage to Luan. Luan died young.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Chou, governor of Guangling and Luan's uncle by marriage, was famous in Han times for his integrity and achievements in office; he gave his daughter to Luan in marriage. Luan died young.

sentences.zh: 又直字伯平，州舉茂才，亦有清名，卒。

translations.literal: Another [son], Zhi, styled Boping, was also nominated as a Prominent Talent by the province and likewise had a reputation for purity. He died.
translations.idiomatic: Another son, Zhi, styled Boping, was likewise recommended as a promising talent by the province and enjoyed a reputation for integrity. He too died.

sentences.zh: 子瑜、儀俱少有至行。

translations.literal: His sons Yu and Yi both showed supreme conduct from youth.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Yu and Yi were both known from boyhood for their exceptional moral conduct.

sentences.zh: 瑜十歲、儀九歲而父亡，居喪毀瘁，過於成人。

translations.literal: Yu was ten and Yi nine when their father died; in mourning they wasted away in grief beyond what adults ordinarily showed.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was ten and Yi nine when their father died. In mourning they grieved themselves nearly to death, more fiercely than grown men.

sentences.zh: 外祖會稽盛孝章，漢末名士也，深加憂傷，每撫慰之，曰：「汝並黃中英爽，終成奇器，何遽逾制自取殄滅邪。」

translations.literal: Their maternal grandfather Sheng Xiaozhang of Kuaiji was a celebrated scholar of late Han and was deeply distressed; he would comfort them, saying, "You are both bright talents in their prime and will surely become extraordinary men—why rush beyond propriety and bring ruin on yourselves?"
translations.idiomatic: Their grandfather on their mother's side, Sheng Xiaozhang of Kuaiji, a celebrated scholar of the late Han, was deeply worried and would comfort them, saying, "You are both gifted young men who will surely become remarkable figures—why exceed the rites of mourning and destroy yourselves?"

sentences.zh: 三年禮畢，殆至滅性，故兄弟並以孝著。

translations.literal: When the three-year mourning was complete they had nearly destroyed themselves, and so the brothers were both famed for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: When the three-year mourning ended they had nearly ruined their health, and both brothers became renowned for filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 瑜早卒。

translations.literal: Yu died young.
translations.idiomatic: Yu died young.

sentences.zh: 儀字仲則，篤學有雅才，以儒素自業。

translations.literal: Yi, styled Zhongze, studied earnestly and had refined talent, taking the Confucian scholar's plain way of life as his vocation.
translations.idiomatic: Yi, styled Zhongze, was a devoted scholar of refined gifts who made the life of a plain Confucian gentleman his calling.

sentences.zh: 時海內大亂，兵革並起，經術廢弛，士少全行。

translations.literal: At the time the realm was in great disorder, arms flared everywhere, classical learning fell into neglect, and few scholars preserved their integrity intact.
translations.idiomatic: The empire was in turmoil, war broke out on every side, classical studies were neglected, and few gentlemen kept their conduct whole.

sentences.zh: 而儀淳深隱默，守道不移，風操貞整，不妄交納，唯與族子仲山、叔山及吳郡陸公紀友善。

translations.literal: Yet Yi was deep, pure, and retiring, holding to the Way without wavering; his conduct was upright and he did not associate casually, befriending only his clansmen Zhongshan and Shushan and Lu Gongji of Wu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Yi remained grave, reserved, and steadfast in the Way. His conduct was impeccable and he made no casual acquaintances, keeping friendship only with his kinsmen Zhongshan and Shushan and with Lu Gongji of Wu.

sentences.zh: 州郡禮請，二府交辟，公車征，並不屈，以壽終。

translations.literal: Provinces and commanderies invited him with ceremony; both regional offices repeatedly summoned him; the imperial carriage office recruited him—all he refused, and he died at the end of his natural span.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial and commandery authorities invited him with full ceremony; both regional headquarters repeatedly called on him; the court sent the imperial carriage to summon him—he declined every offer and died at a full age.

sentences.zh: 子曼字元禪，左中郎、新都都尉、定陽侯，才志顯于吳朝。

translations.literal: His son Man, styled Yuanchan, served as Left Palace Gentleman, Commandant of Xindu, and Marquis of Dingyang; his talent and resolve were conspicuous in the Wu court.
translations.idiomatic: His son Man, styled Yuanchan, became a left palace gentleman, commandant of Xindu, and marquis of Dingyang; his ability and ambition were well known in the kingdom of Wu.

sentences.zh: 子矯字仲桓，以節氣立名，仕為立武校尉、偏將軍。

translations.literal: His son Jiao, styled Zhonghuan, made a name for himself through integrity and spirit; he served as Colonel Who Establishes Martiality and as a lieutenant general.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jiao, styled Zhonghuan, won fame for his integrity and force of character and served as colonel of martial establishment and as lieutenant general.

sentences.zh: 孫皓時，有將帥之稱。

translations.literal: Under Sun Hao he had the reputation of a commander.
translations.idiomatic: Under Sun Hao he was regarded as a capable commander.

sentences.zh: 吳平，為郁林、長沙二郡太守，不就。

translations.literal: When Wu was pacified he was appointed Governor of both Yulin and Changsha but did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall of Wu he was appointed governor of Yulin and Changsha but refused to serve.

sentences.zh: 太康末卒。

translations.literal: He died near the end of the Taikang era.
translations.idiomatic: He died toward the end of the Taikang reign.

sentences.zh: 子陵字景高，晉元帝之為鎮東將軍，命參軍事。

translations.literal: His son Ling, styled Jinggao, when Emperor Yuan of Jin was General Who Guards the East, was appointed a military aide.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ling, styled Jinggao, was made a staff officer when Emperor Yuan of Jin held the post of general who guards the east.

sentences.zh: 子延字思長，潁川太守，始居縣東鄉之博陸里餘烏村。

translations.literal: His son Yan, styled Sichang, was Governor of Yingchuan and first settled in Yuwu Village of Bolu Lane in the county's eastern district.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yan, styled Sichang, became governor of Yingchuan and was the first of the line to settle at Yuwu Village in Bolu Lane, in the eastern part of the county.

sentences.zh: 延子賀字子寧，桓沖南中郎參軍。

translations.literal: Yan's son He, styled Zining, was a military aide to Huan Chong, General of the Southern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's son He, styled Zining, served on the staff of Huan Chong as southern palace general.

sentences.zh: 賀子警字世明，惇篤有行業，學通左氏春秋，家產累千金。

translations.literal: He's son Jing, styled Shiming, was sincere and steadfast with established conduct; he mastered the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals, and his household wealth amounted to several thousand gold pieces.
translations.idiomatic: He's son Jing, styled Shiming, was a man of sincere character and solid achievement who mastered the Zuo tradition of the Spring and Autumn Annals; his family wealth ran to several thousand in gold.

sentences.zh: 後將軍謝安命為參軍，甚相敬重。

translations.literal: General Who Conquers the Rear Xie An appointed him a military aide and greatly respected him.
translations.idiomatic: Xie An, general who conquers the rear, made him a staff officer and held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 警內足於財，為東南豪士，無進仕意，謝病歸。

translations.literal: Jing was inwardly content with his wealth, a magnate of the southeast with no wish to advance in office; he pleaded illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Wealthy enough to need nothing more, Jing was a leading gentleman of the southeast with no ambition for office; he pleaded illness and went home.

sentences.zh: 安固留不止，乃謂曰：「沈參軍，卿有獨善之志，不亦高乎。」

translations.literal: An pressed him to stay but could not detain him, and then said, "Staff Officer Shen, you have the will to perfect yourself alone—is that not lofty?"
translations.idiomatic: An tried hard to keep him but could not; he then said, "Staff Officer Shen, your resolve to cultivate yourself apart from the world—is that not admirable?"

sentences.zh: 警曰：「使君以道禦物，前所以懷德而至，既無用佐時，故遂飲啄之願爾。」

translations.literal: Jing replied, "My lord governs affairs by the Way; that is why I came before out of gratitude for your virtue. Since I have no use in aiding the age, I simply fulfill my wish to eat and drink as nature allows."
translations.idiomatic: Jing replied, "You govern by the Way—that is why I came to you in the first place, moved by your virtue. I have nothing to offer the times, so I am simply following my wish to live quietly as I may."

sentences.zh: 還家積載，以素業自娛。

translations.literal: He returned home with ample stores and amused himself with his plain scholarly pursuits.
translations.idiomatic: He went home with his household goods and devoted himself to the simple life of a scholar.

sentences.zh: 前將軍王恭鎮京口，與警有舊好，復引為參軍。

translations.literal: General of the Van Wang Gong, stationed at Jingkou, had an old friendship with Jing and again brought him in as a military aide.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gong, general of the van, was posted at Jingkou; he and Jing were old friends, and he again took Jing onto his staff.

sentences.zh: 手書殷勤，苦相招致，不得已而應之。

translations.literal: He wrote in his own hand with earnest warmth and pressed him hard to come; unable to refuse, Jing at last accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Gong wrote him a warm letter in his own hand and pressed him insistently; Jing could not refuse and finally agreed.

sentences.zh: 尋復謝去。

translations.literal: Before long he resigned and left again.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he resigned and left once more.

sentences.zh: 子穆夫字彥和，少好學，通左氏春秋。

translations.literal: His son Mufu, styled Yanhe, loved learning from youth and mastered the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: His son Mufu, styled Yanhe, was devoted to study from boyhood and mastered the Zuo tradition of the Spring and Autumn Annals.

sentences.zh: 王恭命為前將軍主簿，謂警曰：「足下既執不拔之志，高臥東南，故屈賢子共事，非吏職嬰之也。」

translations.literal: Wang Gong appointed him chief clerk to the General of the Van and said to Jing, "Since you hold an unyielding resolve and lie high in the southeast, I have humbled myself to ask your worthy son to serve with me—not to bind him with petty clerical duties."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gong made him chief clerk on his staff and told Jing, "You are firm in your resolve to live apart in the southeast, so I have asked your excellent son to work with me—not to trap him in minor clerical work."

sentences.zh: 初，錢唐人杜炅字子恭，通靈有道術，東土豪家及都下貴望並事之為弟子，執在三之敬。

translations.literal: Earlier, Du Jiong of Qiantang, styled Zigong, was versed in spirits and possessed the arts of the Way; great families of the southeast and eminent men of the capital all served him as disciples, observing the reverence due to father, elder brother, and teacher.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Du Jiong of Qiantang, styled Zigong, was believed to communicate with spirits and practiced Daoist arts. Leading families of the southeast and the great men of the capital all became his disciples and treated him with the full deference owed to father, elder brother, and teacher.

sentences.zh: 警累世事道，亦敬事子恭。

translations.literal: For generations the Jing family had served the Way, and Jing likewise revered and served Zigong.
translations.idiomatic: The Jing family had for generations followed the Way, and Jing too honored and served Zigong.

sentences.zh: 子恭死，門徒孫泰、泰弟子恩傳其業，警復事之。

translations.literal: When Zigong died, his disciple Sun Tai and Tai's disciple En carried on his teaching; Jing again served En.
translations.idiomatic: After Zigong's death his disciple Sun Tai, and Tai's disciple En, inherited his teaching; Jing served En as well.

sentences.zh: 隆安三年，恩於會稽作亂，自稱征東將軍，三吳皆回應。

translations.literal: In the third year of Long'an, En rebelled in Kuaiji, styled himself General Who Conquers the East, and all Three Wu regions responded.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Long'an, En rose in rebellion at Kuaiji, proclaimed himself general who conquers the east, and won support throughout the Three Wu region.

sentences.zh: 穆夫在會稽，恩以為余姚令。

translations.literal: Mufu was in Kuaiji, and En appointed him Magistrate of Yuyao.
translations.idiomatic: Mufu was in Kuaiji, and En made him magistrate of Yuyao.

sentences.zh: 及恩為劉牢之所破，穆夫見害。

translations.literal: When En was defeated by Liu Laozhi, Mufu was killed.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Laozhi defeated En, Mufu was put to death.

sentences.zh: 先是穆夫宗人沈預與穆夫父警不協，至是告警及穆夫弟仲夫、任夫、預夫、佩夫，並遇害。

translations.literal: Earlier Mufu's clansman Shen Yu had been at odds with Mufu's father Jing; now he denounced Jing together with Mufu's brothers Zhongfu, Renfu, Yufu, and Peifu, and all were killed.
translations.idiomatic: Mufu's kinsman Shen Yu had long been estranged from Mufu's father Jing; now Yu denounced Jing along with Mufu's brothers Zhongfu, Renfu, Yufu, and Peifu, and all of them were killed.

sentences.zh: 唯穆夫子深子、雲子、田子、林子、虔子獲全。

translations.literal: Only Mufu's sons Shenzi, Yunzi, Tianzi, Linzi, and Qianzi escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: Only Mufu's sons Shenzi, Yunzi, Tianzi, Linzi, and Qianzi survived.

sentences.zh: 田子、林子知名。

translations.literal: Tianzi and Linzi became well known.
translations.idiomatic: Tianzi and Linzi became famous.

sentences.zh: 田子字敬光，從武帝克京城，進平建鄴，參鎮軍事，封營道縣五等侯。

translations.literal: Tianzi, styled Jingguang, followed Emperor Wu in capturing the capital, advanced to pacify Jiankang, served as military aide to the garrison commander, and was enfeoffed as a fifth-rank Marquis of Yingdao County.
translations.idiomatic: Tianzi, styled Jingguang, followed Liu Yu in taking the capital, then helped pacify Jiankang, served on the garrison commander's staff, and was enfeoffed as fifth-rank marquis of Yingdao.

sentences.zh: 帝北伐廣固，田子領偏師與龍驤將軍孟龍符為前鋒。

translations.literal: When the Emperor marched north against Guanggu, Tianzi led a detached force and, with General of Dragon Cavalry Meng Longfu, served as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: On the northern campaign against Guanggu, Tianzi commanded a separate column and, with Meng Longfu, general of dragon cavalry, led the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 龍符戰沒，田子力戰破之。

translations.literal: Longfu fell in battle; Tianzi fought fiercely and routed the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Longfu was killed in battle; Tianzi fought hard and broke the enemy.

sentences.zh: 及盧循逼都，帝遣田子與建威將軍孫季高海道襲破廣州，還除太尉參軍、淮陵內史，賜爵都鄉侯。

translations.literal: When Lu Xun pressed the capital, the Emperor sent Tianzi with General Who Establishes Might Sun Jigao by sea to strike and take Guangzhou; on his return he was appointed military aide to the Grand Commandant and Interior Minister of Huailing, and granted the title Marquis of the Metropolitan District.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Xun threatened the capital, the emperor sent Tianzi with Sun Jigao, general who establishes might, by sea to seize Guangzhou. On his return he was made staff officer to the grand commandant and interior minister of Huailing, and ennobled as marquis of the metropolitan district.

sentences.zh: 義熙八年，從討劉毅。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Yixi he followed the campaign against Liu Yi.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Yixi he took part in the campaign against Liu Yi.

sentences.zh: 十一年，從討司馬休之，除振武將軍、扶風太守。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he followed the campaign against Sima Xiuzhi and was appointed General Who Quells Martiality and Governor of Fufeng.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he joined the campaign against Sima Xiuzhi and was made general who quells martiality and governor of Fufeng.

sentences.zh: 十二年，武帝北伐，田子與順陽太守傅弘之各領別軍，從武關入，屯據青泥。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, on Emperor Wu's northern campaign, Tianzi and Fu Hongzhi, Governor of Shunyang, each led separate armies, entered through Wuguan, and encamped at Qingni.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year, on Liu Yu's northern expedition, Tianzi and Fu Hongzhi, governor of Shunyang, each led independent forces through Wuguan and encamped at Qingni.

sentences.zh: 姚泓將自禦大軍，慮田子襲其後，欲先平田子，然後傾國東出。

translations.literal: Yao Hong was about to face the main army himself, feared Tianzi would strike his rear, wished first to destroy Tianzi, and then move the whole state eastward.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Hong was preparing to meet the main army in person. Fearing Tianzi might attack from the rear, he wanted to eliminate Tianzi first, then march east with his full strength.

sentences.zh: 乃率步騎數萬，奄至青泥。

translations.literal: He therefore led several tens of thousands of infantry and cavalry and suddenly arrived at Qingni.
translations.idiomatic: He led tens of thousands of foot and horse and suddenly appeared at Qingni.

sentences.zh: 田子本為疑兵，所領裁數百，欲擊之。

translations.literal: Tianzi had originally been a decoy force with only a few hundred men under his command, yet he wished to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Tianzi's detachment was meant only as a diversion; he had barely a few hundred men, yet he wanted to attack.

sentences.zh: 傅弘之曰：「彼眾我寡，難可與敵。」

translations.literal: Fu Hongzhi said, "They are many and we are few; it will be hard to meet them in battle."
translations.idiomatic: Fu Hongzhi said, "They outnumber us—we cannot fight them."

sentences.zh: 田子曰：「師貴用奇，不必在眾。」

translations.literal: Tianzi said, "In warfare what matters is the unexpected; numbers are not everything."
translations.idiomatic: Tianzi replied, "Victory depends on surprise, not on numbers alone."

sentences.zh: 弘猶固執，田子曰：「眾寡相傾，勢不兩立，若使賊圍既固，人情喪沮，事便去矣。

translations.literal: Hongzhi still held firm, and Tianzi said, "When many and few confront each other the situation cannot stand divided; if the enemy's encirclement is allowed to tighten and men's spirits collapse, the affair is lost.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi still objected. Tianzi said, "When forces of unequal size meet, only one side can prevail. If we let the enemy complete their encirclement and our men's spirits fail, all is lost.

sentences.zh: 及其未整，薄之必克，所謂先人有奪人之志也。」

translations.literal: Strike them before they are formed up and you are sure to prevail—that is what is meant by seizing the enemy's will before he seizes yours."
translations.idiomatic: Attack before they are ready and we are sure to win—that is what it means to seize the initiative and break the enemy's resolve."

sentences.zh: 便獨率所領，鼓噪而進。

translations.literal: He then led his men alone, advancing with drums and shouts.
translations.idiomatic: He then led his men forward alone, with drums beating and battle cries rising.

sentences.zh: 賊合圍數重，田子乃棄糧毀舍，躬勒士卒，前後奮擊，賊眾一時潰散，所殺萬餘人，得泓偽乘輿服御。

translations.literal: The enemy closed round him in several rings; Tianzi then abandoned grain and burned his quarters, personally drove his soldiers, and struck fiercely fore and aft until the rebel host broke apart at once—more than ten thousand were slain, and he seized Hong's false imperial carriage and regalia.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy surrounded him in layer after layer. Tianzi abandoned his supplies, burned his camp, and personally drove his men to attack from every side until the enemy broke at once. More than ten thousand were killed, and he captured Hong's counterfeit imperial carriage and regalia.

sentences.zh: 武帝表言其狀。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu memorialized the throne reporting what had happened.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu reported the affair to the court in a memorial.

sentences.zh: 長安既平，武帝燕于文昌殿，舉酒賜田子曰：「咸陽之平，卿之功也，即以咸陽相賞。」

translations.literal: When Chang'an was pacified, Emperor Wu feasted in the Wenchang Hall, raised his cup, and granted it to Tianzi, saying, "The pacification of Xianyang is your achievement; let Xianyang be your reward."
translations.idiomatic: After Chang'an was taken, Liu Yu held a feast in the Wenchang Hall, raised his cup to Tianzi, and said, "The fall of Xianyang is your doing—I give you Xianyang as your reward."

sentences.zh: 即授咸陽、始平二郡太守。

translations.literal: He thereupon appointed him Governor of both Xianyang and Shiping.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately made him governor of Xianyang and Shiping.

sentences.zh: 大軍既還，桂陽公義真留鎮長安，以田子為安西中兵參軍、龍驤將軍、始平太守。

translations.literal: After the main army returned, the Prince of Guiyang, Yizhen, remained to garrison Chang'an and appointed Tianzi Central Military Aide of the Pacification of the West, General of Dragon Cavalry, and Governor of Shiping.
translations.idiomatic: When the main army withdrew, Prince of Guiyang Yizhen stayed to garrison Chang'an and made Tianzi central military aide on the western pacification staff, general of dragon cavalry, and governor of Shiping.

sentences.zh: 時赫連勃勃來寇，田子與安西司馬王鎮惡俱出北地禦之。

translations.literal: At the time Helian Bobo came raiding; Tianzi and Wang Zhen'e, military aide of the Pacification of the West, both marched out into Beidi to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: When Helian Bobo invaded, Tianzi and Wang Zhen'e, western pacification marshal, both marched into Beidi to meet him.

sentences.zh: 初，武帝將還，田子及傅弘之等並以鎮惡家在關中，不可保信，屢言之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Emperor Wu was about to return, Tianzi, Fu Hongzhi, and the others all said repeatedly that because Zhen'e's family was in Guanzhong he could not be trusted.
translations.idiomatic: Before Liu Yu withdrew, Tianzi, Fu Hongzhi, and others had repeatedly warned that Zhen'e, whose family remained in Guanzhong, could not be trusted.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「今留卿文武將士、精兵萬人，彼若欲為不善，政足自滅耳。

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "I now leave you civil and military officers and ten thousand picked troops; if he wishes to do wrong, that is enough to bring about his own destruction.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I am leaving you civil and military officers and ten thousand elite troops. If he turns disloyal, that will be enough to destroy him.

sentences.zh: 勿復多言。」

translations.literal: Say no more on the matter."
translations.idiomatic: Say no more about it."

sentences.zh: 及俱出北地，論者謂鎮惡欲盡殺諸南人，以數十人送義真南還，因據關中反叛。

translations.literal: When they all marched out into Beidi, rumor held that Zhen'e intended to kill all the southerners, send only a few dozen men south with Yizhen, and then seize Guanzhong in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: When they marched into Beidi together, people said Zhen'e planned to slaughter all the southerners, send only a few dozen men back south with Yizhen, and then hold Guanzhong in revolt.

sentences.zh: 田子乃于弘之營內請鎮惡計事，使宗人敬仁於坐殺之，率左右數十人自歸義真。

translations.literal: Tianzi then, within Hongzhi's camp, asked Zhen'e to discuss plans, had his clansman Jingren kill him at the meeting, and led several dozen personal followers to surrender himself to Yizhen.
translations.idiomatic: Tianzi asked Zhen'e to discuss plans inside Hongzhi's camp, had his kinsman Jingren kill him at the table, and led a few dozen followers to report to Yizhen.

sentences.zh: 長史王修收殺田子于長安稿倉門外，是歲十四年正月十五日也。

translations.literal: Chief Administrator Wang Xiu seized and executed Tianzi outside the Straw Granary Gate of Chang'an—this was on the fifteenth day of the first month in the fourteenth year.
translations.idiomatic: Chief administrator Wang Xiu arrested and executed Tianzi outside the straw granary gate of Chang'an, on the fifteenth day of the first month of the fourteenth year.

sentences.zh: 武帝表天子以田子卒發狂易，不深罪也。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu memorialized the Son of Heaven that Tianzi had died in a fit of madness and was not to be deeply punished.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu reported to the emperor that Tianzi had died in a sudden fit of madness and asked that he not be severely punished.

sentences.zh: 林子字敬士，少有大度，年數歲，隨王父在京口，王恭見而奇之，曰：「此兒王子師之流也。」

translations.literal: Linzi, styled Jingshi, had great breadth of spirit from youth; when only a few years old he followed his grandfather to Jingkou. Wang Gong saw him and marveled, saying, "This boy is of the same sort as Wang Zishi."
translations.idiomatic: Linzi, styled Jingshi, showed exceptional breadth of character as a boy. When he was only a few years old he went with his grandfather to Jingkou. Wang Gong saw him and was struck by him, saying, "This child is a Wang Zishi in the making."

sentences.zh: 嘗與眾人共見遺寶，咸爭趨之，林子直去不顧。

translations.literal: Once, when he was with others and they came upon abandoned treasure, all rushed to seize it; Linzi walked straight on without a glance.
translations.idiomatic: Once, when he and others came upon treasure left behind, everyone rushed to grab it; Linzi walked straight past without looking.

sentences.zh: 年十三，遇家禍，既門陷祅党，兄弟並應從誅，而沈預家甚強富，志相陷滅，林子兄弟沈伏山澤，無所投厝。

translations.literal: At thirteen he met with family disaster: the household had been implicated with the rebel sect, and the brothers were all liable to execution. Shen Yu's family was very powerful and wealthy and bent on destroying them; Linzi and his brothers hid in mountains and marshes with nowhere to turn.
translations.idiomatic: At thirteen disaster struck his family: implicated in the rebel cult, the brothers were all marked for death. Shen Yu's clan was powerful and wealthy and determined to destroy them; Linzi and his brothers hid in the hills and marshes with nowhere to go.

sentences.zh: 會孫恩屢出會稽，武帝致討，林子乃自歸陳情，率老弱歸罪請命，因流涕哽咽，三軍為之感動。

translations.literal: When Sun En repeatedly emerged from Kuaiji and Emperor Wu marched to punish him, Linzi came forward of his own accord to state his case, leading the old and weak to submit and plead for their lives; he wept and choked with grief, and the whole army was moved.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun En kept raiding from Kuaiji and Liu Yu marched against him, Linzi came forward on his own, led the women, children, and elderly to surrender and plead for mercy, and wept until he could hardly speak; the entire army was moved.

sentences.zh: 帝甚奇之，乃載以別船，遂盡室移京口，帝分宅給焉。

translations.literal: The Emperor was deeply struck by him, had him carried on a separate boat, then moved the whole household to Jingkou and allotted them residences.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly impressed, had him taken on a separate boat, moved the entire family to Jingkou, and gave them houses.

sentences.zh: 林子博覽眾書，留心文義，從克京城，進平都邑。

translations.literal: Linzi read widely in many books and devoted himself to literary meaning; he followed in capturing the capital and advancing to pacify the metropolis.
translations.idiomatic: Linzi read widely and cared deeply for literature and principle; he took part in capturing the capital and pacifying the imperial city.

sentences.zh: 時年十八，身長七尺五寸。

translations.literal: He was then eighteen and stood seven feet five inches in height.
translations.idiomatic: He was eighteen years old and seven feet five inches tall.

sentences.zh: 沈預慮林子為害，常被甲持戈，至是林子與兄田子還東報讎。

translations.literal: Shen Yu feared Linzi would harm him and often wore armor and carried a spear; now Linzi and his brother Tianzi returned east to take revenge.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Yu feared Linzi and often wore armor and carried a weapon; now Linzi and his brother Tianzi went east to settle the score.

sentences.zh: 五月夏節日至，預政大集會，子弟盈堂。

translations.literal: On the summer festival day in the fifth month Yu was holding a great gathering; sons and younger kinsmen filled the hall.
translations.idiomatic: On the summer festival in the fifth month Yu was holding a large family gathering; sons and younger relatives filled the hall.

sentences.zh: 林子兄弟挺身直入，斬預首，男女無論長幼悉屠之，以預首祭父祖墓。

translations.literal: Linzi and his brothers strode straight in, cut off Yu's head, and slaughtered men and women regardless of age; they offered Yu's head at their father and ancestors' tombs.
translations.idiomatic: Linzi and his brothers walked straight in, cut off Yu's head, and killed every man and woman in the house, young and old alike; they offered Yu's head at their father's and ancestors' graves.

sentences.zh: 及帝為揚州，辟為從事，領建熙令，封資中縣五等侯。

translations.literal: When the Emperor became Governor of Yangzhou, he summoned Linzi as an aide, had him concurrently serve as Magistrate of Jianxi, and enfeoffed him as a fifth-rank Marquis of Zizhong County.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yu became governor of Yangzhou, he summoned Linzi as a staff officer, made him magistrate of Jianxi as well, and enfeoffed him as fifth-rank marquis of Zizhong.

sentences.zh: 從伐慕容超，平盧循，並著軍功。

translations.literal: He followed campaigns against Murong Chao and in pacifying Lu Xun, distinguishing himself in both.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in the campaigns against Murong Chao and in suppressing Lu Xun, earning distinction in both.

sentences.zh: 後從征劉毅，參太尉軍事。

translations.literal: Later he followed the campaign against Liu Yi and served as military aide to the Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He later joined the campaign against Liu Yi as staff officer to the grand commandant.

sentences.zh: 復從討司馬休之。

translations.literal: He again followed the campaign against Sima Xiuzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He again took part in the campaign against Sima Xiuzhi.

sentences.zh: 武帝每征討，林子輒推鋒居前。

translations.literal: On every campaign of Emperor Wu, Linzi would thrust forward at the van.
translations.idiomatic: On every expedition Liu Yu undertook, Linzi led the charge at the front.

sentences.zh: 時賊党郭亮之招集蠻、晉，屯據武陵，武陵太守王鎮惡出奔。

translations.literal: At the time the rebel Guo Liangzhi gathered Man and Jin tribesmen, encamped in Wuling, and Wang Zhen'e, Governor of Wuling, fled.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the rebel Guo Liangzhi rallied tribal and Jin forces and held Wuling; Wang Zhen'e, governor of Wuling, fled.

sentences.zh: 林子率軍討之，斬亮之於七里澗而納鎮惡。

translations.literal: Linzi led troops against him, beheaded Liangzhi at Qili Stream, and received Zhen'e back into the district.
translations.idiomatic: Linzi marched against him, killed Liangzhi at Qili Stream, and restored Zhen'e to office.

sentences.zh: 武陵既平，復討魯軌於石城，軌棄眾走襄陽，復追躡之。

translations.literal: When Wuling was pacified he again campaigned against Lu Gui at Shicheng; Gui abandoned his forces and fled to Xiangyang, and Linzi pursued him.
translations.idiomatic: After Wuling was pacified he campaigned against Lu Gui at Shicheng; Gui abandoned his troops and fled to Xiangyang, and Linzi pursued.

sentences.zh: 襄陽既定，權留守江陵。

translations.literal: When Xiangyang was secured, he was left provisionally to garrison Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiangyang was taken, he was left to garrison Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 武帝伐姚泓，復參征西軍事，加建武將軍，統軍為前鋒，從汴入河。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu campaigned against Yao Hong, Linzi again served as military aide on the western expedition, was promoted to General Who Establishes Martiality, commanded the army as vanguard, and entered the Yellow River from the Bian.
translations.idiomatic: On Liu Yu's campaign against Yao Hong, Linzi again served on the western expedition staff, was made general who establishes martiality, commanded the vanguard, and entered the Yellow River from the Bian.

sentences.zh: 偽并州刺史、河東太守尹昭據蒲阪，林子於陝城與冠軍檀道濟同攻蒲阪，龍驤王鎮惡攻潼關。

translations.literal: The false Governor of Bingzhou and Governor of Hedong, Yin Zhao, held Puban; at Shancheng Linzi joined Champion General Tan Daoji in attacking Puban, while Wang Zhen'e, General of Dragon Cavalry, attacked Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Zhao, the Later Qin governor of Bingzhou and Hedong, held Puban. At Shancheng Linzi joined Tan Daoji, champion general, in attacking Puban, while Wang Zhen'e, general of dragon cavalry, assaulted Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 姚泓聞大軍至，遣偽東平公姚紹爭據潼關。

translations.literal: When Yao Hong heard the great army had arrived, he sent the false Prince of Dongping, Yao Shao, to seize Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: When Yao Hong learned the main army was coming, he sent Prince of Dongping Yao Shao to contest Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 林子謂道濟曰：「潼關天岨，所謂形勝之地。

translations.literal: Linzi said to Daoji, "Tong Pass is a natural barrier—the so-called terrain of strategic advantage.
translations.idiomatic: Linzi said to Daoji, "Tong Pass is a natural fortress—the classic strong point.

sentences.zh: 鎮惡孤軍，勢危力屈，若使姚紹據之，則難圖也。

translations.literal: Zhen'e is alone with a perilous, overmatched force; if Yao Shao seizes it, it will be hard to overcome.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen'e is isolated, outnumbered, and hard pressed. If Yao Shao takes the pass, we will never dislodge him.

sentences.zh: 及其未至，當並力爭之。

translations.literal: Before he arrives we must join forces and contest it.
translations.idiomatic: We must combine our strength and seize it before he arrives.

sentences.zh: 若潼關事捷，尹昭可不戰而服。」

translations.literal: If Tong Pass is taken, Yin Zhao can be made to submit without a fight."
translations.idiomatic: If we win at Tong Pass, Yin Zhao will surrender without a battle."

sentences.zh: 道濟從之。

translations.literal: Daoji agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Daoji agreed.

sentences.zh: 及至，紹舉關右之眾，設重圍，圍林子及道濟、鎮惡等。

translations.literal: When they arrived, Shao mustered the forces of Guanxi, set multiple encirclements, and besieged Linzi, Daoji, Zhen'e, and the others.
translations.idiomatic: When they arrived, Shao rallied the armies of the western passes, drew tight rings of encirclement, and surrounded Linzi, Daoji, Zhen'e, and the rest.

sentences.zh: 道濟議欲度河避其鋒，或欲棄捐輜重還赴武帝。

translations.literal: Daoji proposed crossing the river to avoid the enemy's edge, or abandoning baggage and returning to join Emperor Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Daoji proposed crossing the river to escape the enemy's thrust, or abandoning the baggage train and hurrying back to Liu Yu.

sentences.zh: 林子按劍曰：「下官今日之事，自為將軍辦之。

translations.literal: Linzi gripped his sword and said, "What is to be done today, I shall handle for the general myself.
translations.idiomatic: Linzi drew his sword and said, "Today's business I will settle for you myself, General.

sentences.zh: 然二三君子或同業艱難，或荷恩罔極，以此退撓，亦何以見相公旗鼓邪。」

translations.literal: Yet you gentlemen have either shared hardship in the same cause or received boundless grace—if you shrink back now, how will you face our lord's banners?"
translations.idiomatic: Some of you have shared hardship in the same cause, others owe boundless debts of grace—if you flinch now, how can you face our lord's banners?"

sentences.zh: 塞井焚舍，示無全志。

translations.literal: He stopped the wells and burned the quarters, showing there would be no thought of survival.
translations.idiomatic: He had the wells filled in and the camp burned, showing they would fight to the death.

sentences.zh: 率麾下數百人，犯其西北。

translations.literal: He led several hundred men under his command and struck their northwest.
translations.idiomatic: He led several hundred of his men in an assault on their northwest flank.

sentences.zh: 紹眾小靡，乘其亂而薄之，紹乃大潰，俘虜以千數，悉獲紹器械資實。

translations.literal: Shao's troops wavered slightly; taking advantage of the disorder he pressed them, and Shao broke completely—prisoners numbered in the thousands, and all Shao's weapons and stores were captured.
translations.idiomatic: Shao's ranks faltered; Linzi struck while they were in disorder and Shao's army collapsed. Thousands were taken prisoner, and all Shao's arms and supplies were seized.

sentences.zh: 時諸將破賊皆多其首級，而林子獻捷書至，每以實聞。

translations.literal: At the time the other generals defeating the enemy all inflated their head counts, but when Linzi's victory report arrived he always reported the truth.
translations.idiomatic: Other generals inflated their body counts when reporting victories, but Linzi's dispatches always stated the true numbers.

sentences.zh: 武帝問其故，林子曰：「夫王者之師，本有征無戰，豈可復增張虜獲，以示誇誕。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu asked why; Linzi said, "The army of a true king is meant to conquer without fighting—how can we further magnify the enemy's losses to make boastful display?
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yu asked why, Linzi said, "A true king's army conquers without battle—how can we inflate the enemy's losses for the sake of boasting?

sentences.zh: 昔魏尚以盈級受罰，此亦後乘之良轍也。」

translations.literal: In old times Wei Shang was punished for padding his tally—this too is a fine precedent for those who come after."
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shang was once punished for inflating his tally—that is a fine warning for those who come after."

sentences.zh: 武帝曰：「乃所望於卿也。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "That is just what I hoped for from you."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu said, "That is exactly what I expect of you."

sentences.zh: 初，紹退走，還保定城，留偽武衛將軍姚鸞精兵守嶮，林子銜枚夜襲，即屠其城，劓鸞而坑其眾。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Shao had retreated to Baoding, he left the false Martial Guardian General Yao Luan with picked troops to hold the defile; Linzi attacked by night with gags in the men's mouths, took the city at once, cut off Luan's nose, and buried his men alive.
translations.idiomatic: When Shao had retreated to Baoding he left Yao Luan, false martial guardian general, with elite troops to hold the pass. Linzi attacked by night with muffled mouths, stormed the city, cut off Luan's nose, and buried his troops alive.

sentences.zh: 紹復遣撫軍將軍姚贊將兵屯河上，林子連破之。

translations.literal: Shao again sent the Pacifying Army General Yao Zan with troops encamped on the river; Linzi defeated him repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: Shao sent Pacifying Army General Yao Zan to hold the river; Linzi defeated him again and again.

sentences.zh: 紹又遣長史姚伯子等屯據九泉，憑河固險，以絕糧援。

translations.literal: Shao also sent Chief Administrator Yao Bozi and others to hold Jiuchuan, relying on the river's strength to cut off grain supplies.
translations.idiomatic: Shao also sent chief administrator Yao Bozi and others to hold Jiuchuan, using the river's defenses to sever their grain route.

sentences.zh: 武帝復遣林子累戰大破之，即斬伯子，所俘獲悉以還紹，使知王師之弘。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu sent Linzi to fight again and he won a great victory, beheaded Bozi, and returned all captives to Shao to show him the magnanimity of the royal army.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu sent Linzi to fight again; he won a great victory, beheaded Bozi, and returned all prisoners to Shao to show the mercy of the imperial army.

sentences.zh: 紹志節沈勇，林子每戰輒勝，白武帝曰：「姚紹氣蓋關右而力以勢屈，但恐凶命先盡，不得以釁齊斧爾。」

translations.literal: Shao was resolute, deep, and brave; Linzi won every battle and reported to Emperor Wu, "Yao Shao's spirit covers Guanxi but his strength is bent by circumstance—I only fear his ill fate will end first and he will not live to meet the imperial axe."
translations.idiomatic: Shao was resolute and formidable; Linzi won every engagement and told Liu Yu, "Yao Shao's spirit dominates the western passes, but his strength is failing—I only fear he will die before he can face the imperial axe."

sentences.zh: 尋紹疽發背死。

translations.literal: Before long Shao died of a carbuncle on his back.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Shao died of a carbuncle on his back.

sentences.zh: 武帝以林子之驗，乃賜書嘉美之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu, because Linzi's prediction had been fulfilled, sent a letter praising him.
translations.idiomatic: Because Linzi's prediction had come true, Liu Yu sent him a letter of praise.

sentences.zh: 於是贊統後軍復襲林子，林子禦之，連戰皆捷。

translations.literal: Then Zan took command of the rear army and again attacked Linzi; Linzi resisted and won successive victories.
translations.idiomatic: Zan then commanded the rear army and attacked Linzi again; Linzi held him off and won every engagement.

sentences.zh: 帝至閿鄉，姚泓掃境內兵屯嶢柳。

translations.literal: When the Emperor reached Wenxiang, Yao Hong swept the realm's forces to encamp at Yaoliu.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yu reached Wenxiang, Yao Hong gathered the realm's armies and encamped at Yaoliu.

sentences.zh: 時田子自武關北入，屯軍藍田，泓自率大眾攻之。

translations.literal: At the time Tianzi had entered from the north through Wuguan and encamped at Lantian; Hong led the main force himself to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Tianzi had entered from the north through Wuguan and encamped at Lantian; Hong led his main force in person to attack him.

sentences.zh: 帝慮眾寡不敵，遣林子步自秦嶺以相接援。

translations.literal: The Emperor feared they could not match the enemy in numbers and sent Linzi by foot from the Qin Mountains to link up in support.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Tianzi was outnumbered, Liu Yu sent Linzi overland from the Qin Mountains to reinforce him.

sentences.zh: 比至，泓已破走。

translations.literal: By the time he arrived, Hong had already been defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: By the time Linzi arrived, Hong had already been beaten and had fled.

sentences.zh: 田子欲窮追，進取長安，林子止之曰：「往取長安，如指掌爾。

translations.literal: Tianzi wished to pursue to the end and take Chang'an; Linzi stopped him, saying, "To take Chang'an now would be as easy as pointing to the palm of your hand.
translations.idiomatic: Tianzi wanted to pursue and seize Chang'an; Linzi stopped him, saying, "Taking Chang'an now would be as easy as turning over your hand.

sentences.zh: 復克賊城，便為獨平一國，不賞之功也。」

translations.literal: If you also capture the enemy's cities, you will have pacified a whole state alone—an achievement that cannot be rewarded."
translations.idiomatic: If you capture more enemy cities you will have pacified a whole realm by yourself—an achievement too great to reward."

sentences.zh: 田子乃止。

translations.literal: Tianzi then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Tianzi desisted.

sentences.zh: 林子威震關中，豪右望風請附。

translations.literal: Linzi's prestige shook Guanzhong; the powerful gentry submitted at the mere rumor of his approach.
translations.idiomatic: Linzi's prestige shook Guanzhong; the great families submitted at the mere report of his name.

sentences.zh: 帝以林子、田子綏略有方，頻賜書褒美，並令深慰納之。

translations.literal: The Emperor, because Linzi and Tianzi had pacified and governed effectively, repeatedly sent letters of praise and ordered them to comfort and win over the people.
translations.idiomatic: Because Linzi and Tianzi had governed effectively, Liu Yu repeatedly praised them in letters and ordered them to win the people over.

sentences.zh: 長安既平，姚氏十餘萬口西奔隴上，林子追討至寡婦水，轉鬥至槐里。

translations.literal: When Chang'an was pacified, more than a hundred thousand of the Yao clan fled west into Long; Linzi pursued to Widow's Water and fought on to Huaili.
translations.idiomatic: After Chang'an fell, more than a hundred thousand of the Yao clan fled west into Long; Linzi pursued to Widow's Water and fought on to Huaili.

sentences.zh: 大軍東歸，林子領水軍于石門以為聲援。

translations.literal: When the main army marched east, Linzi led the navy at Shimen as a supporting force.
translations.idiomatic: When the main army withdrew east, Linzi commanded the fleet at Shimen as a rear guard.

sentences.zh: 還至彭城，帝令林子差次勳勤，隨才授用。

translations.literal: On returning to Pengcheng, the Emperor had Linzi rank merit and assign posts according to each man's ability.
translations.idiomatic: Back at Pengcheng, Liu Yu had Linzi rank the men by merit and assign offices according to their abilities.

sentences.zh: 文帝出鎮荊州，議以林子及謝晦為蕃佐。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen went out to garrison Jingzhou, it was proposed that Linzi and Xie Hui serve as frontier aides.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen went out to garrison Jingzhou, some proposed Linzi and Xie Hui as his frontier aides.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「吾不可頓無二人，林子行則晦不宜出。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "I cannot suddenly be without both men; if Linzi goes, Hui should not leave."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu said, "I cannot be without both of them at once; if Linzi goes, Hui must stay."

sentences.zh: 乃以林子為西中郎中兵參軍，領新興太守。

translations.literal: He therefore appointed Linzi Central Military Aide of the Western Palace and concurrently Governor of Xinxing.
translations.idiomatic: He made Linzi central military aide of the western palace and concurrently governor of Xinxing.

sentences.zh: 林子以行役久，士有歸心，乃深陳事宜。

translations.literal: Linzi, because the troops had been on campaign so long that the men longed for home, set forth the situation in depth.
translations.idiomatic: Because the troops had been on campaign so long that the men longed to return, Linzi laid out the situation at length.

sentences.zh: 並言：「聖王所以戒慎祗肅，非以崇威立武，實乃經國長甿。

translations.literal: He also said, "The reason the sage kings are reverent and cautious is not to exalt might and establish arms, but truly to govern the state and nurture the people for the long term.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Sage kings are reverent and cautious not to glorify military power, but to govern the state and secure the people for generations.

sentences.zh: 宜廣建蕃屏，崇嚴宿衛。」

translations.literal: Screen principalities should be broadly established and the palace guard strengthened."
translations.idiomatic: Principalities should be broadly established and the palace guard strengthened."

sentences.zh: 武帝深相酬納。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu responded to him deeply and accepted his counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu responded warmly and accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 俄而謝翼謀反，帝歎曰：「林子之見，何其明也。」

translations.literal: Before long Xie Yi rebelled; the Emperor sighed, "How clear-sighted Linzi's judgment was."
translations.idiomatic: Soon Xie Yi rebelled; Liu Yu sighed, "How clear Linzi was."

sentences.zh: 文帝進號鎮西，隨府轉，加建威將軍、河東太守。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen advanced his title to General Who Pacifies the West, Linzi followed the headquarters and was promoted to General Who Establishes Martiality and Governor of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen was made general who pacifies the west, Linzi followed his staff and was promoted to general who establishes martiality and governor of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 時武帝以方隅未靜，復欲親戎，林子固諫。

translations.literal: At the time Emperor Wu, because the borders were not yet quiet, wished again to take the field in person; Linzi firmly remonstrated.
translations.idiomatic: The borders were still unsettled and Liu Yu wished to campaign in person again; Linzi firmly dissuaded him.

sentences.zh: 帝答曰：「吾輒當不復自行。」

translations.literal: The Emperor answered, "I shall probably not take the field myself again."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu answered, "I shall probably not campaign in person again."

sentences.zh: 帝踐阼，以佐命功，封漢壽縣伯，固讓不許。

translations.literal: When the Emperor ascended the throne, for his merit in aiding the founding he was enfeoffed as Baron of Hanshou County; he firmly declined but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yu took the throne, Linzi was enfeoffed as baron of Hanshou for his founding merit; he declined firmly but was not allowed.

sentences.zh: 永初三年卒，追贈征虜將軍。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongchu he died; posthumously he was made General Who Punishes the Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third year of Yongchu and was posthumously made general who punishes the barbarians.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十五年，諡曰懷。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year of Yuanjia his posthumous title was Huaai.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year of Yuanjia he was given the posthumous name Huaai.

sentences.zh: 少子璞嗣。

translations.literal: His youngest son Pu succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His youngest son Pu succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 璞字道真，童孺時神意閑審。

translations.literal: Pu, styled Daozhen, even as a child showed a calm and discerning spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Pu, styled Daozhen, showed a calm, discerning spirit even as a child.

sentences.zh: 文帝召見，奇璞應對，謂林子曰：「此非常兒也。」

translations.literal: Emperor Wen summoned him; marveling at Pu's replies, he said to Linzi, "This is no ordinary boy."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen summoned him; struck by Pu's replies, he told Linzi, "This is no ordinary child."

sentences.zh: 初除南平王左常侍，文帝引見，謂之曰：「吾昔以弱年出蕃，卿家以親要見輔，今日之授，意在不薄。

translations.literal: At his first appointment as Left Attendant to the Prince of Nanping, the Emperor received him and said, "In my youth I went out to a frontier principality and your family assisted me through close ties—today's appointment is not meant to be slight.
translations.idiomatic: At his first appointment as left attendant to the Prince of Nanping, the emperor received him and said, "When I was young I went out to a frontier principality and your family aided me through close ties—today's appointment is not meant lightly.

sentences.zh: 王家之事，一以相委。

translations.literal: Matters of the princely household are entirely entrusted to you.
translations.idiomatic: All affairs of the princely household are entrusted to you.

sentences.zh: 勿以國官乖清塗為罔罔也。」

translations.literal: Do not let the state office obscure the clear path."
translations.idiomatic: Do not let your state office blind you to what is right."

sentences.zh: 元嘉十七年，始興王浚為揚州刺史，寵愛殊異，以為主簿。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Yuanjia, when the Prince of Shixing Jun was made Governor of Yangzhou and favored with exceptional intimacy, Pu was made his chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year of Yuanjia, when Prince of Shixing Jun became governor of Yangzhou and was favored with exceptional intimacy, Pu was made his chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 時順陽范曄為長史行州事，曄性頗疏，文帝謂璞曰：「范曄性疏，必多不同，卿腹心所寄，當密以在意。

translations.literal: At the time Fan Ye of Shunyang was chief administrator acting for the province; Ye was rather careless in temperament, and the Emperor told Pu, "Fan Ye is careless by nature and will surely differ with you often—you are the one in whom I place my trust, and you must keep this secretly in mind.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Ye of Shunyang was chief administrator acting for the province; Ye was rather careless, and the emperor told Pu, "Fan Ye is careless by nature and will often disagree with you—you are the one I trust; keep this firmly in mind.

sentences.zh: 彼行事，其實卿也。」

translations.literal: Whatever he does, in truth it is you who act.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever he does, in truth it is you who act.

sentences.zh: 璞以任遇既深，所懷輒以密啟，每至施行，必從中出。

translations.literal: Because Pu's favor and trust were so deep, whatever he thought he reported in secret; whenever anything was carried out, it always came from his counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Because Pu's trust was so deep, he reported his thoughts in secret; whenever policy was enacted, it came from his counsel.

sentences.zh: 曄政謂聖明留察，故深更恭慎，而莫見其際也。

translations.literal: Ye believed the sage ruler was watching closely, and therefore became still more respectful and cautious, yet never saw how things really worked.
translations.idiomatic: Ye believed the sage ruler was watching closely and became still more respectful, never seeing how things really worked.

sentences.zh: 在職八年，神州大寧，人無謗黷，璞有力焉。

translations.literal: In eight years of office the central realm was greatly at peace and no one spoke ill of him—Pu had a large share in this.
translations.idiomatic: In eight years of office the realm was greatly at peace and no one spoke ill of the administration—Pu had much to do with it.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，范曄坐事誅，時浚雖曰親覽，州事一以付璞。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year Fan Ye was executed for an offense; though Jun now said he oversaw affairs himself, all provincial business was entrusted to Pu.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year Fan Ye was executed; though Jun said he oversaw affairs himself, all provincial business went to Pu.

sentences.zh: 浚年既長，璞固求辭事。

translations.literal: Jun was already grown; Pu firmly asked to be relieved of duty.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was already grown; Pu firmly asked to be relieved.

sentences.zh: 以璞為浚始興國大農，累遷淮南太守。

translations.literal: Pu was made Grand Agriculturist of Jun's Principality of Shixing and was repeatedly promoted to Governor of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: He was made grand agriculturist of Jun's principality of Shixing and later promoted to governor of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 三十年，元凶弑立，璞以奉迎之晚見殺。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year the crown prince usurped and murdered; Pu was killed because his welcome had come too late.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year the crown prince murdered his father and usurped the throne; Pu was killed because he had been slow to welcome the new regime.

sentences.zh: 有子曰約，其制自序大略如此。

translations.literal: He had a son Yue; his own preface gives the outline of the clan history much as this.
translations.idiomatic: He had a son Yue; Yue's own preface gives much the same outline of the clan history.

sentences.zh: 約十三而遭家難，潛竄，會赦乃免。

translations.literal: Yue was thirteen when disaster struck his family; he went into hiding and was spared only when an amnesty was declared.
translations.idiomatic: Yue was thirteen when disaster struck his family; he went into hiding and was spared only when an amnesty was declared.

sentences.zh: 既而流寓孤貧，篤志好學，晝夜不釋卷。

translations.literal: Afterward he wandered in poverty and isolation, devoted himself to study, and never put down his books day or night.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward he wandered in poverty and isolation, devoted himself to study, and never put down his books day or night.

sentences.zh: 母恐其以勞生疾，常遣減油滅火。

translations.literal: His mother, fearing overwork would bring illness, often had the lamp oil reduced and the fire lowered.
translations.idiomatic: His mother, fearing overwork would bring illness, often had the lamp oil reduced and the fire lowered.

sentences.zh: 而晝之所讀，夜輒誦之，遂博通群籍，善屬文。

translations.literal: What he read by day he recited by night, and so he mastered all the classics and excelled at literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: What he read by day he recited by night, until he had mastered the classics and excelled at writing.

sentences.zh: 濟陽蔡興宗聞其才而善之，及為郢州，引為安西外兵參軍，兼記室。

translations.literal: Cai Xingzong of Jiyang heard of his talent and favored him; when he became Governor of Yingzhou he brought Yue in as Western Pacification Outer Military Aide and concurrently Recorder.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Xingzong of Jiyang heard of his talent and favored him; when he became governor of Yingzhou he made Yue western pacification outer military aide and recorder.

sentences.zh: 興宗常謂其諸子曰：「沈記室人倫師表，宜善師之。」

translations.literal: Xingzong often told his sons, "Recorder Shen is a model of human conduct—you should study under him well."
translations.idiomatic: Xingzong often told his sons, "Recorder Shen is a model of human conduct—you should learn from him."

sentences.zh: 及為荊州，又為征西記室，帶厥西令。

translations.literal: When he became Governor of Jingzhou, Yue again served as Recorder on the western expedition staff and concurrently Magistrate of Juexi.
translations.idiomatic: When he became governor of Jingzhou, Yue again served as recorder on the western expedition staff and as magistrate of Juexi.

sentences.zh: 齊初為征虜記室，帶襄陽令，所奉主即齊文惠太子。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qi he was Recorder on the staff of the General Who Punishes the Barbarians and concurrently Magistrate of Xiangyang; the lord he served was the Qi heir Wenhuizi.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Qi he was recorder on the staff of the general who punishes the barbarians and magistrate of Xiangyang; his lord was the Qi heir Wenhuizi.

sentences.zh: 太子入居東宮，為步兵校尉，管書記，直永壽省，校四部圖書。

translations.literal: When the heir entered the Eastern Palace, Yue became Colonel of Footsoldiers, managed documents, served at the Yongshou Office, and collated the four sections of the imperial library.
translations.idiomatic: When the heir entered the eastern palace, Yue became colonel of footsoldiers, managed documents, served at the Yongshou Office, and collated the four sections of the imperial library.

sentences.zh: 時東宮多士，約特被親遇，每旦入見，景斜方出。

translations.literal: At the time the Eastern Palace had many men of talent, but Yue was especially favored; each morning he entered to see the heir and only left when the sun was slanting.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern palace had many talented men, but Yue was especially favored; each morning he entered and only left when the sun was low.

sentences.zh: 時王侯到宮或不得進，約每以為言。

translations.literal: At times princes and nobles coming to the palace could not gain entry, but Yue always spoke on their behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes princes and nobles could not gain entry, but Yue always spoke for them.

sentences.zh: 太子曰：「吾生平懶起，是卿所悉，得卿談論，然後忘寢。

translations.literal: The heir said, "By nature I am lazy about rising—that is something you know well; only when I talk with you do I forget sleep.
translations.idiomatic: The heir said, "I am lazy about rising by nature—you know that; only when I talk with you do I forget sleep.

sentences.zh: 卿欲我夙興，可恒早入。」

translations.literal: If you wish me to rise early, you may always come in early."
translations.idiomatic: If you want me to rise early, come in early every day."

sentences.zh: 遷太子家令。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Household Master of the Heir.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to household master of the heir.

sentences.zh: 後為司徒右長史、黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: Later he became Right Chief Administrator of the Secretariat and Attendant of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Later he became right chief administrator of the secretariat and attendant of the yellow gate.

sentences.zh: 時竟陵王招士，約與蘭陵蕭琛、琅邪王融、陳郡謝朓、南鄉范雲、樂安任昉等皆遊焉。

translations.literal: At the time the Prince of Jingling was gathering scholars; Yue joined Xiao Chen of Lanling, Wang Rong of Langye, Xie Tiao of Chen, Fan Yun of Nanxiang, Ren Fang of Le'an, and others in his circle.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jingling was gathering scholars; Yue joined Xiao Chen of Lanling, Wang Rong of Langye, Xie Tiao of Chen, Fan Yun of Nanxiang, Ren Fang of Le'an, and others in his circle.

sentences.zh: 當世號為得人。

translations.literal: They were called the finest gathering of the age.
translations.idiomatic: They were called the finest gathering of the age.

sentences.zh: 初，梁武在西邸，與約遊舊。

translations.literal: Earlier, Emperor Wu of Liang, while at the western residence, had been an old companion of Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Emperor Wu of Liang, while at the western residence, had been an old companion of Yue.

sentences.zh: 建康城平，引為驃騎司馬。

translations.literal: When Jiankang was pacified he was brought in as military aide to the Flying Cavalry General.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiankang was pacified he was brought in as military aide to the flying cavalry general.

sentences.zh: 時帝勳業既就，天人允屬。

translations.literal: At the time the Emperor's achievement was already complete and both Heaven and men were in accord.
translations.idiomatic: By then the emperor's achievement was complete and both Heaven and men were in accord.

sentences.zh: 約嘗扣其端，帝默然而不應。

translations.literal: Yue once probed his intentions; the Emperor remained silent and did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Yue once probed his intentions; the emperor remained silent.

sentences.zh: 佗日又進曰：「今與古異，不可以淳風期萬物。

translations.literal: Another day he advanced again and said, "Present and past differ—one cannot expect all things by the standards of pure antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Another day he pressed again: "Present and past differ—one cannot expect the world to live by the standards of pure antiquity.

sentences.zh: 士大夫攀龍附鳳者，皆望有尺寸之功，以保其福祿。

translations.literal: Scholars and officials who climb the dragon and cling to the phoenix all hope for some small merit to preserve their fortune and rank.
translations.idiomatic: Officials who attach themselves to rising power all hope for some small merit to preserve their fortune and rank.

sentences.zh: 今童兒牧豎悉知齊祚之終，且天文人事表革運之征，永元以來，尤為彰著。

translations.literal: Today even children and shepherds know the Qi mandate is ending, and the signs of a change in fate in Heaven and among men are especially clear since Yongyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Today even children and shepherds know the Qi mandate is ending, and the signs of a change of fate in Heaven and among men have been especially clear since Yongyuan.

sentences.zh: 讖云：『行中水，作天子』。

translations.literal: A prophecy says, "Moving within water, one becomes Son of Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: A prophecy says, "Moving within water, one becomes Son of Heaven."

sentences.zh: 此又歷然在記。

translations.literal: This too is plainly recorded in the chronicles.
translations.idiomatic: This too is plainly recorded in the chronicles.

sentences.zh: 天心不可違，人情不可失。」

translations.literal: Heaven's will cannot be opposed, and human sentiment cannot be lost."
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's will cannot be opposed, and human sentiment cannot be ignored."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「吾方思之。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "I am still considering it."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I am still considering it."

sentences.zh: 約曰：「公初起兵樊、沔，此時應思。

translations.literal: Yue said, "When you first raised arms at Fan and Mian, that was the time to consider it.
translations.idiomatic: Yue said, "When you first raised arms at Fan and Mian, that was the time to consider it.

sentences.zh: 今日王業已就，何所復思。

translations.literal: Today the royal enterprise is already achieved—what is left to consider?
translations.idiomatic: Today the royal enterprise is achieved—what is left to consider?

sentences.zh: 昔武王伐紂，始入人便曰吾君。

translations.literal: In old times when King Wu attacked Zhou, as soon as he entered the people's territory they said "Our lord."
translations.idiomatic: When King Wu attacked Zhou, as soon as he entered the people's territory they called him their lord.

sentences.zh: 武王不違人意，亦無所思。

translations.literal: King Wu did not go against the people's will and had nothing to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: King Wu did not go against the people's will and had nothing to deliberate.

sentences.zh: 公自至京邑，已移氣序，比于周武，遲速不同。

translations.literal: Since you yourself reached the capital the temper of the times has shifted; compared with King Wu of Zhou, the pace differs.
translations.idiomatic: Since you reached the capital the temper of the times has shifted; compared with King Wu, you have been slower.

sentences.zh: 若不早定大業，稽天人之望，脫一人立異，便損威德。

translations.literal: If you do not settle the great enterprise early and align with Heaven and men's expectations, should someone else raise a different banner, your prestige and virtue will suffer.
translations.idiomatic: If you do not settle the great enterprise early and align with Heaven and men's expectations, should someone else raise a banner, your prestige will suffer.

sentences.zh: 且人非金石，時事難保，豈可以建安之封，遺之子孫。

translations.literal: Moreover, men are not metal or stone and the times are hard to guarantee—how can you leave the fief of Jian'an to your descendants?
translations.idiomatic: Men are not metal or stone and times are uncertain—how can you leave the fief of Jian'an to your descendants?

sentences.zh: 若天子還都，公卿在位，則君臣分定，無復異圖。

translations.literal: If the Son of Heaven returns to the capital and the lords and ministers take their places, then the roles of ruler and subject are fixed and there will be no further designs.
translations.idiomatic: If the Son of Heaven returns to the capital and the lords and ministers take their places, ruler and subject will be fixed and there will be no further designs.

sentences.zh: 君明於上，臣忠於下，豈復有人方更同公作賊。」

translations.literal: The ruler is enlightened above and the ministers loyal below—how could anyone again join you in rebellion?"
translations.idiomatic: With an enlightened ruler above and loyal ministers below, who could again join you in rebellion?"

sentences.zh: 帝然之。

translations.literal: The Emperor agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 約出，召範雲告之，雲對略同約旨。

translations.literal: When Yue went out he summoned Fan Yun and told him; Yun's reply largely matched Yue's intent.
translations.idiomatic: When Yue left he summoned Fan Yun and told him; Yun's reply largely matched Yue's intent.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「智者乃爾暗同，卿明早將休文更來。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "Wise men agree in secret like this—tomorrow morning bring Xiufen again."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Wise men think alike in secret—bring Xiufen again tomorrow morning."

sentences.zh: 雲出語約，約曰：「卿必待我。」

translations.literal: When Yun went out he told Yue; Yue said, "You must wait for me."
translations.idiomatic: Yun told Yue outside; Yue said, "You must wait for me."

sentences.zh: 雲許諾。

translations.literal: Yun promised.
translations.idiomatic: Yun agreed.

sentences.zh: 而約先期入，帝令草其事。

translations.literal: But Yue entered first; the Emperor ordered him to draft the matter.
translations.idiomatic: But Yue went in first; the emperor ordered him to draft the arrangements.

sentences.zh: 約乃出懷中詔書並諸選置，帝初無所改。

translations.literal: Yue then produced from his bosom the edict and all appointments; at first the Emperor changed nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Yue produced from his sleeve the edict and all appointments; the emperor changed nothing.

sentences.zh: 俄而雲自外來，至殿門不得入，徘徊壽光合外，但云：「咄咄」。

translations.literal: Before long Yun came from outside; reaching the palace gate he could not enter, and paced outside the Shouguang Hall compound, saying only, "Alas, alas."
translations.idiomatic: Soon Yun arrived from outside; he could not enter the palace gate and paced outside the Shouguang Hall, muttering only, "Alas, alas."

sentences.zh: 約出，雲問曰：「何以見處？」

translations.literal: When Yue came out, Yun asked, "How was I treated?"
translations.idiomatic: When Yue came out, Yun asked, "How was I treated?"

sentences.zh: 約舉手向左，雲笑曰：「不乖所望。」

translations.literal: Yue raised his hand to the left; Yun laughed and said, "Not contrary to what I expected."
translations.idiomatic: Yue pointed to the left; Yun laughed and said, "Just as I expected."

sentences.zh: 有頃，帝召雲謂曰：「生平與沈休文群居，不覺有異人處，今日才智縱橫，可謂明識。」

translations.literal: After a while the Emperor summoned Yun and said, "In life I lived with Shen Xiufen in company and never noticed anything extraordinary about him; today his talent and wisdom range freely—this may be called clear insight."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Yun and said, "I lived with Shen Xiufen for years and never noticed anything extraordinary; today his talent ranges freely—truly clear insight."

sentences.zh: 雲曰：「公今知約，不異約今知公。」

translations.literal: Yun said, "Your Majesty now knows Yue—no different from Yue now knowing Your Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: Yun said, "Your Majesty now knows Yue—no different from Yue now knowing you."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「我起兵於今三年矣，功臣諸將實有其勞，然成帝業者乃卿二人也。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "I have raised arms for three years now; the meritorious generals have indeed labored, yet those who accomplished the imperial enterprise are you two alone."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I have campaigned for three years; my generals have indeed labored, yet those who accomplished the imperial enterprise are you two alone."

sentences.zh: 梁台建，為散騎常侍、吏部尚書，兼右僕射。

translations.literal: When the Liang headquarters was established, he was made Attendant Cavalier, Minister of the Civil Service, and concurrently Right Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liang headquarters was established, he became attendant cavalier, minister of the civil service, and concurrently right vice director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 及受禪，為尚書僕射，封建昌縣侯。

translations.literal: Upon receiving the abdication he was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and enfeoffed as Marquis of Jianchang.
translations.idiomatic: Upon receiving the abdication he became vice director of the secretariat and was enfeoffed as marquis of Jianchang.

sentences.zh: 又拜約母謝為建昌國太夫人。

translations.literal: The Emperor also ennobled Yue's mother Xie as Grand Lady of Jianchang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also ennobled Yue's mother Xie as grand lady of Jianchang.

sentences.zh: 奉策之日，吏部尚書范雲等二十餘人咸來致拜，朝野以為榮。

translations.literal: On the day the edict was presented, more than twenty men including Fan Yun, Minister of the Civil Service, came to pay homage; court and commoners alike regarded it as an honor.
translations.idiomatic: On the day the edict was presented, more than twenty men including Fan Yun, minister of the civil service, came to pay homage; court and commoners regarded it as an honor.

sentences.zh: 俄遷左僕射。

translations.literal: Before long he was promoted to Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to left vice director.

sentences.zh: 天監二年，遭母憂，輿駕親出臨吊，以約年衰，不宜致毀，遣中書舍人斷客節哭。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianjian he met with his mother's death; the imperial carriage came in person to mourn, and because Yue was aged and should not destroy himself, an aide was sent to cut off visitors and regulate mourning.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianjian his mother died; the emperor came in person to mourn. Because Yue was old and should not ruin his health, an aide was sent to regulate visitors and mourning.

sentences.zh: 起為鎮軍將軍、丹陽尹，置佐史。

translations.literal: He was recalled as General Who Pacifies the Army and Governor of Danyang, with staff officers appointed.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as general who pacifies the army and governor of Danyang, with staff officers appointed.

sentences.zh: 服闋，遷侍中、右光祿大夫，領太子詹事，奏尚書八條事。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was promoted to Palace Attendant and Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, concurrently Grand Tutor of the Heir, and memorialized eight items for the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he became palace attendant and right grand master of splendid happiness, concurrently grand tutor of the heir, and memorialized eight items for the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書令，累表陳讓，改授左僕射，領中書令。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Director of the Secretariat, repeatedly memorialized to decline, and was instead made Left Vice Director, concurrently Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to director of the secretariat, repeatedly declined, and was instead made left vice director, concurrently director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 尋遷尚書令，領太子少傅。

translations.literal: Before long he was again Director of the Secretariat and concurrently Junior Tutor of the Heir.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was again director of the secretariat and junior tutor of the heir.

sentences.zh: 九年，轉左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was transferred to Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was transferred to left grand master of splendid happiness.

sentences.zh: 初，約久處端揆，有志台司，論者咸謂為宜。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yue had long held the highest offices and aspired to the Three Excellencies; commentators all said it was fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Yue had long held the highest offices and aspired to the Three Excellencies; everyone said it was fitting.

sentences.zh: 而帝終不用，乃求外出，又不見許。

translations.literal: Yet the Emperor never appointed him; he then sought to go out on assignment and was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the emperor never appointed him; he sought an outside post and was refused.

sentences.zh: 與徐勉素善，遂以書陳情於勉，言己老病，「百日數旬，革帶常應移孔；

translations.literal: He was on good terms with Xu Mian and therefore wrote to Mian stating his feelings, saying he was old and ill: "For a hundred days, several tens of them—the leather belt must constantly be moved a hole;
translations.idiomatic: He was on good terms with Xu Mian and wrote to him, saying he was old and ill: "For a hundred days, several tens of them—the belt must constantly be moved a hole;

sentences.zh: 以手握臂，率計月小半分」。

translations.literal: grasping the arm with the hand, on average a little less than half a finger a month."
translations.idiomatic: grasping the arm with the hand, on average a little less than half a finger a month."

sentences.zh: 欲謝事，求歸老之秩。

translations.literal: He wished to resign office and seek the rank of retirement.
translations.idiomatic: He wished to resign and seek retirement rank.

sentences.zh: 勉為言於帝，請三司之儀，弗許，但加鼓吹而已。

translations.literal: Mian spoke to the Emperor on his behalf, requesting the honors of the Three Excellencies; this was not granted, and only ceremonial music was added.
translations.idiomatic: Mian spoke to the emperor on his behalf, requesting the honors of the Three Excellencies; this was refused, and only ceremonial music was added.

sentences.zh: 約性不飲酒，少嗜欲，雖時遇隆重，而居處儉素。

translations.literal: Yue did not drink wine and had few desires; though he met with great favor, his dwelling remained plain.
translations.idiomatic: Yue did not drink and had few desires; though greatly honored, his dwelling remained plain.

sentences.zh: 立宅東田，矚望郊阜，常為郊居賦以序其事。

translations.literal: He built a house in the eastern fields, gazing at the suburban heights, and often wrote a Rhapsody on Suburban Living to describe it.
translations.idiomatic: He built a house in the eastern fields overlooking the suburban heights and wrote a Rhapsody on Suburban Living to describe it.

sentences.zh: 尋加特進，遷中軍將軍、丹陽尹，侍中、特進如故。

translations.literal: Before long he was given special advancement and promoted to General of the Central Army and Governor of Danyang, remaining Palace Attendant and specially advanced as before.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was given special advancement and made general of the central army and governor of Danyang, remaining palace attendant and specially advanced as before.

sentences.zh: 十二年卒官，年七十三，諡曰隱。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he died in office at seventy-three; his posthumous title was Yin.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he died in office at seventy-three; his posthumous title was Yin.

sentences.zh: 約左目重瞳子，腰有紫志，聰明過人，好墳籍，聚書至二萬卷，都下無比。

translations.literal: Yue had a double pupil in his left eye and a purple mark on his waist; his intelligence surpassed others. He loved ancient texts and collected books to twenty thousand scrolls, unmatched in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Yue had a double pupil in his left eye and a purple mark on his waist; his intelligence surpassed others. He loved ancient texts and collected twenty thousand scrolls, unmatched in the capital.

sentences.zh: 少孤貧，約幹宗党得米數百斛，為宗人所侮，覆米而去。

translations.literal: In youth he was orphaned and poor; Yue managed clan affairs and obtained several hundred bushels of rice, but was insulted by clansmen and overturned the rice and left.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was orphaned and poor; he managed clan affairs and obtained several hundred bushels of rice, but was insulted by clansmen and overturned the rice and left.

sentences.zh: 及貴不以為憾，用為郡部傳。

translations.literal: When he became eminent he bore no resentment and used the story in a commandery and district biography.
translations.idiomatic: When eminent he bore no resentment and used the story in a local biography.

sentences.zh: 嘗侍宴，有妓婢師是齊文惠宮人，帝問識座中客不？

translations.literal: Once when attending a feast, a singing girl had been a palace woman of Qi Wenhuizi; the Emperor asked whether she recognized any guest at the table.
translations.idiomatic: Once at a feast a singing girl had been a palace woman of Qi Wenhuizi; the emperor asked whether she recognized anyone.

sentences.zh: 曰：「唯識沈家令。」

translations.literal: She said, "I only recognize the Director of the Secretariat of the Shen family."
translations.idiomatic: She said, "I only recognize Director Shen."

sentences.zh: 約伏地流涕，帝亦悲焉，為之罷酒。

translations.literal: Yue prostrated himself and wept; the Emperor was also grieved and stopped the wine.
translations.idiomatic: Yue prostrated himself and wept; the emperor was grieved and stopped the feast.

sentences.zh: 約曆仕三代，該悉舊章，博物洽聞，當世取則。

translations.literal: Yue served through three dynasties, mastered old regulations, was broadly learned and well informed, and was the standard of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Yue served three dynasties, mastered old regulations, was broadly learned, and was the standard of the age.

sentences.zh: 謝玄暉善為詩，任彥升工於筆，約兼而有之，然不能過也。

translations.literal: Xie Xuancheng excelled at poetry and Ren Yansheng at prose; Yue had both, yet could surpass neither.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Xuancheng excelled at poetry and Ren Yansheng at prose; Yue had both, yet surpassed neither.

sentences.zh: 自負高才，昧于榮利，乘時射勢，頗累清談。

translations.literal: Confident in his high talent yet blind to glory and profit, he seized the moment and shot for position, and in pure discourse he was rather encumbered.
translations.idiomatic: Confident in his talent yet blind to glory and profit, he seized the moment for position and his pure talk suffered for it.

sentences.zh: 及居端揆，稍弘止足，每進一官，輒殷勤請退，而終不能去，論者方之山濤。

translations.literal: When he reached the highest office he became somewhat more content to stop, and each time he advanced a rank he earnestly asked to retire—yet in the end he could not leave; commentators compared him to Shan Tao.
translations.idiomatic: At the summit he became somewhat more willing to stop; each promotion he asked to retire—yet could not leave; commentators compared him to Shan Tao.

sentences.zh: 用事十餘年，未常有所薦達，政之得失，唯唯而已。

translations.literal: In more than ten years of power he never recommended anyone for advancement; on whether government was right or wrong he only assented.
translations.idiomatic: In more than ten years of power he never recommended anyone; on government right or wrong he only assented.

sentences.zh: 初，武帝有憾于張稷，及卒，因與約言之。

translations.literal: Earlier the Emperor had resentment toward Zhang Ji; when Ji died he spoke of it with Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the emperor resented Zhang Ji; when Ji died he spoke of it with Yue.

sentences.zh: 約曰：「左僕射出作邊州刺史，已往之事，何足復論。」

translations.literal: Yue said, "The Left Vice Director went out as frontier governor; past matters—what is there to discuss again?"
translations.idiomatic: Yue said, "The left vice director went out as frontier governor; past matters—what is there to discuss?"

sentences.zh: 帝以為約昏家相為，怒約曰：「卿言如此，是忠臣邪！」
