translations.literal: The Emperor thought Yue was covering for his in-laws and angrily said, "If you speak like this, are you a loyal minister?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thought Yue was covering for in-laws and angrily said, "If you speak like this, are you a loyal minister?"

sentences.zh: 乃輦歸內殿。

translations.literal: He then returned to the inner palace by carriage.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to the inner palace by carriage.

sentences.zh: 約懼，不覺帝起，猶坐如初。

translations.literal: Yue was afraid and did not notice the Emperor rising, still sitting as before.
translations.idiomatic: Yue was afraid and did not notice the emperor rising, still sitting as before.

sentences.zh: 及還，未至床，憑空頓於戶下，因病。

translations.literal: When the Emperor returned, before reaching the couch Yue fell abruptly at the doorway and fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned, before reaching the couch Yue fell at the doorway and fell ill.

sentences.zh: 夢齊和帝劍斷其舌，召巫視之，巫言如夢。

translations.literal: He dreamed that the sword of Emperor He of Qi cut off his tongue; he summoned a shaman, who said it was as in the dream.
translations.idiomatic: He dreamed Emperor He of Qi's sword cut off his tongue; a shaman said it matched the dream.

sentences.zh: 乃呼道士奏赤章於天，稱禪代之事，不由己出。

translations.literal: He then had a Daoist present a red petition to Heaven, saying the matter of the abdication was not of his own will.
translations.idiomatic: He had a Daoist present a red petition to Heaven, saying the abdication was not his own will.

sentences.zh: 先此，約嘗侍宴，會豫州獻栗，徑寸半。

translations.literal: Before this, when Yue once attended a feast, Yuzhou presented chestnuts an inch and a half across.
translations.idiomatic: Before this, at a feast Yuzhou presented chestnuts an inch and a half across.

sentences.zh: 帝奇之，問栗事多少，與約各疏所憶，少帝三事。

translations.literal: The Emperor marveled and asked how many chestnut matters each recalled; Yue was three items short of the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor marveled and asked how many chestnut matters each recalled; Yue was three short of the emperor.

sentences.zh: 約出謂人曰：「此公護前，不讓即羞死。」

translations.literal: When Yue went out he told others, "This lord protects his lead—if one does not yield he would die of shame."
translations.idiomatic: When Yue went out he said, "This lord protects his lead—if one does not yield he would die of shame."

sentences.zh: 帝以其言不遜，欲抵其罪，徐勉固諫乃止。

translations.literal: The Emperor, because his words were disrespectful, wished to punish him; Xu Mian firmly remonstrated and he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to punish him for disrespect; Xu Mian firmly dissuaded him and he stopped.

sentences.zh: 及疾，上遣主書黃穆之專知省視，穆之夕還，增損不即啟聞，懼罪，竊以赤章事因上省醫徐奘以聞，又積前失。

translations.literal: When he fell ill the Emperor sent the chief clerk Huang Muzhi solely to observe him; Muzhi returned each evening without reporting changes at once, fearing guilt, and secretly reported the red petition matter through the physician Xu Zang—adding to prior faults.
translations.idiomatic: When ill the emperor sent Huang Muzhi to observe him; Muzhi returned each evening without reporting at once, fearing guilt, and secretly reported the red petition through physician Xu Zang—adding to prior faults.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，中使譴責者數焉，約懼遂卒。

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly angered; imperial envoys reproached him several times, and Yue died in fear.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly angered; envoys reproached him several times, and Yue died in fear.

sentences.zh: 有司諡曰：「文」，帝曰：「懷情不盡曰隱」，故改為隱。

translations.literal: The office proposed the posthumous title Wen; the Emperor said, "Cherishing feeling without exhausting it is called Yin," and therefore changed it to Yin.
translations.idiomatic: The office proposed Wen; the emperor said, "Cherishing feeling without exhausting it is called Yin," and changed it to Yin.

sentences.zh: 約少時常以晉氏一代竟無全書，年二十許，便有撰述之意。

translations.literal: In youth Yue often thought the Jin house lacked a complete history for a whole dynasty; at about twenty he had the intention to compose one.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Yue thought the Jin house lacked a complete history; at about twenty he intended to compose one.

sentences.zh: 宋泰始初，征西將軍蔡興宗為啟，明帝有敕許焉。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song Taishi, General Who Pacifies the West Cai Xingzong memorialized on his behalf, and Emperor Ming issued an edict permitting it.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Song Taishi, Cai Xingzong memorialized on his behalf, and Emperor Ming permitted it.

sentences.zh: 自此踰二十年，所撰之書方就，凡一百餘卷。

translations.literal: From then more than twenty years passed before the book he composed was finished, more than a hundred scrolls in all.
translations.idiomatic: More than twenty years passed before the book was finished, more than a hundred scrolls in all.

sentences.zh: 條流雖舉，而采綴未周。

translations.literal: The categories were set forth but the gathering of materials was not yet complete.
translations.idiomatic: The categories were set forth but the gathering of materials was not yet complete.

sentences.zh: 永明初遇盜，失第五帙。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongming it met with thieves and the fifth fascicle was lost.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yongming thieves stole it and the fifth fascicle was lost.

sentences.zh: 又齊建元四年被敕撰國史，永明二年又兼著作郎，撰次起居注。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Qi Jianyuan he was ordered to compile the national history; in the second year of Yongming he was also Compiler and drafted the Daily Records.
translations.idiomatic: In Qi Jianyuan year four he was ordered to compile the national history; in Yongming year two he was also compiler and drafted the Daily Records.

sentences.zh: 五年春又被敕撰宋書，六年二月畢功，表上之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of spring he was again ordered to compile the History of Song; in the second month of the sixth year the work was finished and presented.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of the fifth year he was ordered to compile the History of Song; in the second month of the sixth year it was finished and presented.

sentences.zh: 其所撰國史為齊紀二十卷。

translations.literal: The national history he compiled was the Qi Annals in twenty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: The national history he compiled was the Qi Annals in twenty scrolls.

sentences.zh: 天監中，又撰梁武紀十四卷，又撰邇言十卷，諡例十卷，文章志三十卷，文集一百卷，皆行於世。

translations.literal: Under Tianjian he also compiled the Liang Wudi Annals in fourteen scrolls, also compiled Recent Words in ten scrolls, Posthumous Examples in ten scrolls, Literary Records in thirty scrolls, and Collected Works in a hundred scrolls—all circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tianjian he compiled the Liang Wudi Annals in fourteen scrolls, Recent Words in ten, Posthumous Examples in ten, Literary Records in thirty, and Collected Works in a hundred—all circulated.

sentences.zh: 又撰四聲譜，以為「在昔詞人累千載而不悟，而獨得胸衿，窮其妙旨」。

translations.literal: He also compiled a Treatise on the Four Tones, holding that "past poets for a thousand years did not understand, yet I alone grasped it in my breast and exhausted its subtle intent."
translations.idiomatic: He compiled a Treatise on the Four Tones, holding that "past poets for a thousand years did not understand, yet I alone grasped its subtle intent."

sentences.zh: 自謂入神之作。

translations.literal: He considered it a work that entered the divine.
translations.idiomatic: He considered it divinely inspired.

sentences.zh: 武帝雅不好焉，嘗問周舍曰：「何謂四聲？」

translations.literal: Emperor Wu by nature did not care for it and once asked Zhou She, "What are the four tones?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu did not care for it and once asked Zhou She, "What are the four tones?"

sentences.zh: 舍曰：「'天子聖哲'是也。」

translations.literal: She said, "'The Son of Heaven is sage and wise' is an example."
translations.idiomatic: She said, "'The Son of Heaven is sage and wise' is an example."

sentences.zh: 然帝竟不甚遵用約也。

translations.literal: Yet the Emperor in the end did not greatly follow Yue's usage.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the emperor did not greatly follow Yue's usage.

sentences.zh: 子旋，字士規，襲爵，位司徒右長史，太子僕。

translations.literal: His son Xuan, styled Shigui, inherited the title and served as Right Chief Administrator of the Secretariat and Palace Steward.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xuan, styled Shigui, inherited the title and served as right chief administrator of the secretariat and palace steward.

sentences.zh: 以母憂去官，因蔬食辟穀，服除，猶絕粳粱。

translations.literal: He left office for his mother's mourning, then ate vegetables and avoided grain; when mourning ended he still abstained from polished grain.
translations.idiomatic: He left office for mourning, ate vegetables and avoided grain; when mourning ended he still abstained from polished grain.

sentences.zh: 終於南康內史，諡曰恭。

translations.literal: He ended as Interior Minister of Nankang; his posthumous title was Gong.
translations.idiomatic: He died as interior minister of Nankang; his posthumous title was Gong.

sentences.zh: 集注邇言，行於世。

translations.literal: He compiled a commentary on Recent Words that circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled a commentary on Recent Words that circulated.

sentences.zh: 旋弟趨字孝鯉，亦知名，位黃門郎。

translations.literal: Xuan's younger brother Qu, styled Xiaoli, was also well known and served as Attendant of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan's younger brother Qu, styled Xiaoli, was also well known and served as attendant of the yellow gate.

sentences.zh: 旋卒，子寔嗣。

translations.literal: When Xuan died, his son Shi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuan died, his son Shi succeeded.

sentences.zh: 寔弟眾。

translations.literal: Shi's younger brother Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: Shi's younger brother was Zhong.

sentences.zh: 眾字仲師，好學，頗有文詞。

translations.literal: Zhong, styled Zhongshi, loved learning and had considerable literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong, styled Zhongshi, loved learning and had literary talent.

sentences.zh: 仕梁為太子舍人。

translations.literal: He served Liang as Attendant of the Heir.
translations.idiomatic: He served Liang as attendant of the heir.

sentences.zh: 時梁武帝制千文詩，眾為之注解。

translations.literal: At the time Emperor Wu of Liang composed a Thousand-Character Poem, and Zhong wrote a commentary on it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang composed a Thousand-Character Poem, and Zhong wrote a commentary.

sentences.zh: 與陳郡謝景同時召見於文德殿，帝令眾為竹賦。

translations.literal: He and Xie Jing of Chen were summoned together to the Wende Hall; the Emperor had Zhong compose a rhapsody on bamboo.
translations.idiomatic: He and Xie Jing of Chen were summoned to the Wende Hall; the emperor had Zhong compose a rhapsody on bamboo.

sentences.zh: 賦成奏之，手敕答曰：「卿文體翩翩，可謂無忝爾祖。」

translations.literal: When the rhapsody was finished and presented, the Emperor wrote in his own hand, "Your literary manner is graceful—you do not disgrace your ancestor."
translations.idiomatic: When it was presented, the emperor wrote, "Your literary manner is graceful—you do not disgrace your ancestor."

sentences.zh: 累遷太子中舍人，兼散騎常侍，聘魏，還為驃騎廬陵王諮議參軍。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Attendant of the Heir and concurrently Attendant Cavalier, was envoy to Wei, and on return became military aide to the Flying Cavalry General, Prince of Luling.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to attendant of the heir and concurrently attendant cavalier, envoy to Wei, and on return military aide to the flying cavalry general, Prince of Luling.

sentences.zh: 侯景之亂，表求還吳興召募故義部曲以討賊，梁武許之。

translations.literal: During Hou Jing's rebellion he memorialized asking to return to Wuxing to summon his old righteous followers to fight the bandits; Emperor Wu of Liang permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: During Hou Jing's rebellion he asked to return to Wuxing to summon old followers to fight the rebels; Liang Wu permitted it.

sentences.zh: 及景圍台城，眾率宗族及義附五千餘人入援都，軍容甚整，景深憚之。

translations.literal: When Jing besieged the capital, Zhong led clansmen and righteous followers, more than five thousand, to aid the capital; his army was very orderly and Jing deeply feared him.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing besieged the capital, Zhong led clansmen and followers, more than five thousand, to aid the capital; his army was orderly and Jing deeply feared him.

sentences.zh: 梁武於城內遙授太子右衛率。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang from within the city remotely appointed him Right Commandant of the Heir's Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Wu from within the city appointed him right commandant of the heir's guard.

sentences.zh: 臺城陷，眾乃降景。

translations.literal: When the capital fell, Zhong then surrendered to Jing.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital fell, Zhong surrendered to Jing.

sentences.zh: 景平，元帝以為司徒左長史。

translations.literal: When Jing was pacified, Emperor Yuan made him Left Chief Administrator of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing was pacified, Emperor Yuan made him left chief administrator of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 魏克江陵，見虜，尋亦逃歸。

translations.literal: When Wei took Jiangling he was captured, but soon escaped and returned.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei took Jiangling he was captured, but soon escaped and returned.

sentences.zh: 陳武帝受命，位中書令。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Chen received the mandate he served as Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Wu received the mandate he served as director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 帝以眾州裏知名，甚敬重之，賞賜超于時輩。

translations.literal: The Emperor, because Zhong was well known in his home province, greatly respected him and rewarded him beyond his contemporaries.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, because Zhong was well known at home, greatly respected him and rewarded him beyond his peers.

sentences.zh: 性吝嗇，財帛億計，無所分遺。

translations.literal: By nature he was stingy; his wealth ran to hundreds of millions yet he gave nothing away.
translations.idiomatic: By nature stingy, his wealth ran to hundreds of millions yet he gave nothing away.

sentences.zh: 自奉甚薄，每朝會中，衣裳破裂，或躬提冠履。

translations.literal: His own fare was very spare; at court his clothes were torn, and sometimes he carried his cap and shoes himself.
translations.idiomatic: His own fare was spare; at court his clothes were torn, and sometimes he carried his cap and shoes himself.

sentences.zh: 永定二年，兼起部尚書，監起太極殿。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongding he was concurrently Minister of Works overseeing construction and supervised the building of the Hall of Supreme Pole.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongding he was concurrently minister of works overseeing construction of the Hall of Supreme Pole.

sentences.zh: 恒服布袍芒屩，以麻繩為帶，又囊麥飯鉡以噉之，朝士咸共誚其所為。

translations.literal: He always wore cloth robes and straw sandals, used hemp rope for a belt, and carried a bag of wheat meal and a ladle to eat it; court gentlemen all mocked his conduct.
translations.idiomatic: He wore cloth robes and straw sandals, used hemp rope for a belt, and carried wheat meal in a bag with a ladle; court gentlemen mocked him.

sentences.zh: 眾性狷急，因忿恨，遂曆詆公卿，非毀朝廷。

translations.literal: Zhong was by nature impatient; in resentment he slandered lords and ministers and vilified the court.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong was impatient; in resentment he slandered lords and ministers and vilified the court.

sentences.zh: 武帝大怒，以眾素有令望，不欲顯誅，因其休假還武康，遂于吳中賜死。

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly angered; because Zhong had long enjoyed a good reputation he did not wish to execute him openly, and when Zhong took leave to return to Wukang he had him ordered to die in Wu.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly angered; because Zhong had long enjoyed a good reputation he did not wish to execute him openly, and when Zhong took leave to Wukang had him ordered to die in Wu.

sentences.zh: 范雲字彥龍，南鄉舞陰人，晉平北將軍汪六世孫也。

translations.literal: Fan Yun, styled Yanlong, was a man of Wuyin in Nanxiang, sixth-generation descendant of Jin General Who Pacifies the North Fan Wang.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Yun, styled Yanlong, was from Wuyin in Nanxiang, sixth-generation descendant of Jin general who pacifies the north Fan Wang.

sentences.zh: 祖璩之，宋中書侍郎。

translations.literal: His grandfather Qiong served as Attendant of the Secretariat in Song.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Qiong served as attendant of the secretariat under Song.

sentences.zh: 雲六歲就其姑夫袁叔明讀毛詩，日誦九紙。

translations.literal: At six Yun went to his uncle by marriage Yuan Shuming to study the Mao version of the Book of Songs, reciting nine sheets a day.
translations.idiomatic: At six he studied the Mao Book of Songs with his uncle by marriage Yuan Shuming, reciting nine sheets a day.

sentences.zh: 陳郡殷琰名知人，候叔明見之，曰：「公輔才也」。

translations.literal: Yin Yan of Chen Commandery was famed for knowing men; waiting on Shuming he saw Yun and said, "Material for chief minister."
translations.idiomatic: Yin Yan of Chen, famed for judging men, saw Yun and said, "Material for chief minister."

sentences.zh: 雲性機警，有識具，善屬文，下筆輒成，時人每疑其宿構。

translations.literal: Yun was by nature alert and discerning, skilled at literary composition; when he took up the brush it was finished at once, and people often suspected he had prepared it overnight.
translations.idiomatic: Yun was alert and discerning, skilled at writing; his compositions flowed at once, and people often suspected overnight preparation.

sentences.zh: 父抗為郢府參軍，雲隨在郢。

translations.literal: His father Kang was a military aide in the Ying headquarters; Yun followed him in Ying.
translations.idiomatic: His father Kang was staff officer in the Ying headquarters; Yun followed him there.

sentences.zh: 時吳興沈約、新野庾杲之與抗同府，見而友之。

translations.literal: At the time Shen Yue of Wuxing and Yu Gaozhi of Xinye were in the same office as Kang and befriended him upon meeting him.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Yue of Wuxing and Yu Gaozhi of Xinye were in the same office as Kang and befriended Yun.

sentences.zh: 起家郢州西曹書佐，轉法曹行參軍。

translations.literal: He began his career as Western Bureau Clerk of Yingzhou, then transferred to Acting Military Aide in the Law Section.
translations.idiomatic: He began as western bureau clerk of Yingzhou, then became acting military aide in the law section.

sentences.zh: 俄而沈攸之舉兵圍郢城，抗時為府長流，入城固守，留家屬居外。

translations.literal: Before long Shen Youzhi raised troops and besieged Yingcheng; Kang was then chief administrator of the headquarters, entered the city to hold firm, and left his family outside.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Shen Youzhi besieged Yingcheng; Kang entered to hold the city and left his family outside.

sentences.zh: 雲為軍人所得，攸之召與語，聲色甚厲。

translations.literal: Yun was taken by Youzhi's soldiers; Youzhi summoned and spoke with him, his voice and manner very fierce.
translations.idiomatic: Yun was captured; Youzhi summoned him and spoke fiercely.

sentences.zh: 雲容貌不變，徐自陳說。

translations.literal: Yun's countenance did not change; he slowly stated his case.
translations.idiomatic: Yun's expression did not change; he calmly stated his case.

sentences.zh: 攸之笑曰：「卿定可兒，且出就舍。」

translations.literal: Youzhi laughed and said, "You are surely a fine fellow—go out to quarters for now."
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi laughed and said, "You are a fine fellow—go to quarters for now."

sentences.zh: 明旦又召雲令送書入城內，餉武陵王酒一石，犢一頭；

translations.literal: The next morning he again summoned Yun and ordered him to deliver a letter into the city, presenting the Prince of Wuling with a stone of wine and a calf;
translations.idiomatic: Next morning he summoned Yun to deliver a letter into the city, with a stone of wine and a calf for the Prince of Wuling;

sentences.zh: 餉長史柳世隆鱠魚二十頭，皆去其首。

translations.literal: presenting Chief Administrator Liu Shilong with twenty sliced fish, all beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: and twenty sliced fish, all beheaded, for chief administrator Liu Shilong.

sentences.zh: 城內或欲誅雲，雲曰：「老母弱弟，懸命沈氏。

translations.literal: Some within the city wished to execute Yun; Yun said, "My old mother and weak younger brother hang on the Shen clan's fate.
translations.idiomatic: Some in the city wished to kill Yun; he said, "My mother and younger brother hang on the Shen clan's fate.

sentences.zh: 若其違命，禍必及親。

translations.literal: If I disobey the order, disaster will reach my kin.
translations.idiomatic: If I disobey, disaster will reach my kin.

sentences.zh: 今日就戮，甘心如薺。」

translations.literal: To die today would be sweet as shepherd's purse to my heart."
translations.idiomatic: To die today would be sweet to my heart."

sentences.zh: 世隆素與雲善，乃免之。

translations.literal: Shilong had long been friendly with Yun and therefore spared him.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong, long friendly with Yun, spared him.

sentences.zh: 後除員外散騎郎。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Outer Attendant Cavalier.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was appointed outer attendant cavalier.

sentences.zh: 齊建元初，竟陵王子良為會稽太守，雲為府主簿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qi Jianyuan, Prince of Jingling Ziliang was Governor of Kuaiji and Yun was chief clerk of the headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Qi Jianyuan, Prince of Jingling Ziliang was governor of Kuaiji and Yun was his chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 王未之知。

translations.literal: The prince did not yet know him.
translations.idiomatic: The prince did not yet know him.

sentences.zh: 後克日登秦望山，乃命云。

translations.literal: Later on the day set for ascending Mount Qinwang he ordered Yun to attend.
translations.idiomatic: Later on the day set for ascending Mount Qinwang he ordered Yun to attend.

sentences.zh: 雲以山上有秦始皇刻石，此文三句一韻，人多作兩句讀之，並不得韻；

translations.literal: Yun knew that on the mountain was an inscription of Qin Shihuang; the text rhymed in lines of three, and most people read it in lines of two and could not get the rhyme;
translations.idiomatic: Yun knew Qin Shihuang's inscription was on the mountain; it rhymed in threes, and most read it in twos and missed the rhyme;

sentences.zh: 又皆大篆，人多不識，乃夜取史記讀之令上口。

translations.literal: moreover it was all in great seal script, which most did not know, so he took the Records of the Historian at night and read until it was fluent on the tongue.
translations.idiomatic: moreover it was in great seal script, which most could not read, so he studied the Records of the Historian overnight until he could recite it.

sentences.zh: 明日登山，子良令賓僚讀之，皆茫然不識。

translations.literal: The next day ascending the mountain, Ziliang had the guests read it; all were blankly ignorant.
translations.idiomatic: Next day on the mountain, Ziliang had guests read it; none could.

sentences.zh: 末問雲，雲曰：「下官嘗讀史記，見此刻石文。」

translations.literal: Last he asked Yun; Yun said, "Your servant once read the Records of the Historian and saw this inscribed text."
translations.idiomatic: Last he asked Yun; Yun said, "I once read this text in the Records of the Historian."

sentences.zh: 乃進讀之如流。

translations.literal: He then read it fluently.
translations.idiomatic: He read it fluently.

sentences.zh: 子良大悅，因以為上賓。

translations.literal: Ziliang was greatly pleased and made him a chief guest.
translations.idiomatic: Ziliang was greatly pleased and made him a chief guest.

sentences.zh: 自是寵冠府朝。

translations.literal: From then his favor topped the headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: From then his favor topped the headquarters.

sentences.zh: 王為丹陽尹，復為主簿，深相親任。

translations.literal: When the prince became Governor of Danyang, Yun again served as chief clerk and was deeply trusted.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince became governor of Danyang, Yun again served as chief clerk and was deeply trusted.

sentences.zh: 時進見齊高帝，會有獻白烏，帝問此何瑞，雲位卑最後答，曰：「臣聞王者敬宗廟則白烏至。」

translations.literal: Once when advancing to an audience with Emperor Gao of Qi, a white crow was presented; the Emperor asked what omen this was; Yun, lowest in rank, answered last, saying, "Your servant hears that when a king reveres the ancestral temple the white crow comes."
translations.idiomatic: Once at audience with Emperor Gao of Qi, a white crow was presented; the emperor asked the omen; Yun, lowest in rank, answered last: "When a king reveres the ancestral temple, the white crow comes."

sentences.zh: 時謁廟始畢，帝曰：「卿言是也。

translations.literal: At the time the temple visit had just ended; the Emperor said, "Your words are correct.
translations.idiomatic: The temple visit had just ended; the emperor said, "You are correct.

sentences.zh: 感應之理，一至此乎。」

translations.literal: The principle of response can reach this far."
translations.idiomatic: Response can reach this far."

sentences.zh: 子良為南徐州、南兗州，雲並隨府遷，每陳朝政得失於子良。

translations.literal: When Ziliang was in southern Xuzhou and southern Yanzhou, Yun followed the headquarters in each transfer and often stated the gains and losses of court policy to Ziliang.
translations.idiomatic: When Ziliang held southern Xuzhou and Yanzhou, Yun followed and often advised him on court policy.

sentences.zh: 尋除尚書殿中郎。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Palace Gentleman of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed palace gentleman of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 子良為雲求祿，齊武帝曰：「聞範雲諂事汝，政當流之。」

translations.literal: Ziliang sought an office for Yun; Emperor Wu of Qi said, "I hear Fan Yun flatters you—he ought to be banished."
translations.idiomatic: Ziliang sought an office for Yun; Emperor Wu of Qi said, "I hear Fan Yun flatters you—he ought to be banished."

sentences.zh: 子良對曰：「雲之事臣，動相箴諫，諫書存者百有餘紙。」

translations.literal: Ziliang replied, "In serving me Yun always admonishes; more than a hundred remonstrance letters remain."
translations.idiomatic: Ziliang replied, "Yun always admonishes me; more than a hundred remonstrance letters remain."

sentences.zh: 帝索視之，言皆切至，咨嗟良久，曰：「不意范雲乃爾，方令弼汝。」

translations.literal: The Emperor asked to see them; the words were all incisive; he sighed long and said, "I did not expect Fan Yun to be like this—let him assist you."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read them; all were incisive; he sighed and said, "I did not expect this—let him assist you."

sentences.zh: 子良為司徒，又補記室。

translations.literal: When Ziliang became Minister of the Secretariat, Yun was again appointed Recorder.
translations.idiomatic: When Ziliang became minister of the secretariat, Yun was again appointed recorder.

sentences.zh: 時巴東王子響在荊州，殺上佐，都下匈匈，人多異志。

translations.literal: At the time the Prince of Badong Zixiang was in Jingzhou and killed his chief aide; the capital was in turmoil and many harbored different designs.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Badong Zixiang in Jingzhou killed his chief aide; the capital was in turmoil and many harbored different designs.

sentences.zh: 而豫章王嶷鎮東府，多還私邸，動移旬日。

translations.literal: Prince of Yuzhang Yi garrisoned the eastern headquarters but often returned to private residences, sometimes for ten-day stretches.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Yuzhang Yi garrisoned the eastern headquarters but often returned home for ten-day stretches.

sentences.zh: 子良築第西郊，遊戲而已。

translations.literal: Ziliang built a mansion in the western suburbs and only played.
translations.idiomatic: Ziliang built a mansion in the western suburbs and only played.

sentences.zh: 而梁武帝時為南郡王文學，與雲俱為子良所禮。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang was then literary aide to the Prince of Nan Commandery and, with Yun, was honored by Ziliang.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Wu was then literary aide to the Prince of Nan and, with Yun, was honored by Ziliang.

sentences.zh: 梁武勸子良還石頭，並言大司馬宜還東府，子良不納。

translations.literal: Liang Wu urged Ziliang to return to Stone City and also said the Grand Marshal should return to the eastern headquarters; Ziliang did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Wu urged Ziliang to return to Stone City and said the grand marshal should return to the eastern headquarters; Ziliang refused.

sentences.zh: 梁武以告云。

translations.literal: Liang Wu told Yun.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Wu told Yun.

sentences.zh: 時廷尉平王植為齊武帝所狎，雲謂植曰：「西夏不靜，人情甚惡，大司馬詎得久還私第？

translations.literal: At the time Wang Zhi, assistant director of the Court of Justice, was favored by Emperor Wu of Qi; Yun said to Zhi, "The western border is unsettled and popular sentiment is very bad—how can the Grand Marshal long remain at his private residence?
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhi, assistant director of the court of justice, was favored by Qi Wu; Yun said, "The western border is unsettled and sentiment is bad—how can the grand marshal stay at home?

sentences.zh: 司徒亦宜鎮石頭。

translations.literal: The Minister of the Secretariat should also garrison Stone City.
translations.idiomatic: The minister of the secretariat should also garrison Stone City.

sentences.zh: 卿入既數，言之差易。」

translations.literal: You enter audience often—speaking would be easier."
translations.idiomatic: You enter audience often—speaking would be easier."

sentences.zh: 植因求雲作啟自呈之。

translations.literal: Zhi therefore asked Yun to draft a memorial and presented it himself.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi asked Yun to draft a memorial and presented it.

sentences.zh: 俄而二王各鎮一城。

translations.literal: Before long both princes each garrisoned a city.
translations.idiomatic: Soon both princes each garrisoned a city.

sentences.zh: 文惠太子嘗幸東田觀獲稻，雲時從。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Wenhuizi once visited the eastern fields to watch the rice harvest; Yun was in attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Wenhuizi once watched the rice harvest in the eastern fields; Yun attended.

sentences.zh: 文惠顧雲曰：「此刈甚快。」

translations.literal: Wenhuizi turned to Yun and said, "This reaping is very quick."
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince said to Yun, "This reaping is very quick."

sentences.zh: 雲曰：「三時之務，亦甚勤勞，願殿下知稼穡之艱難，無徇一朝之宴逸也。」

translations.literal: Yun said, "The labors of the three seasons are also very toilsome; I wish Your Highness would know the hardship of farming and not indulge a morning's ease."
translations.idiomatic: Yun said, "The three seasons are toilsome; I wish Your Highness knew farming's hardship and did not indulge a morning's ease."

sentences.zh: 文惠改容謝之。

translations.literal: Wenhuizi changed expression and apologized.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince changed expression and apologized.

sentences.zh: 及出，侍中蕭緬先不相識，就車握雲手曰：「不謂今日復見讜言。」

translations.literal: When they left, Palace Attendant Xiao Mian, who had not known Yun before, took his hand at the carriage and said, "I did not expect to hear remonstrance again today."
translations.idiomatic: Palace attendant Xiao Mian, who had not known Yun, took his hand and said, "I did not expect remonstrance today."

sentences.zh: 永明十年使魏，魏使李彪宣命，至雲所，甚見稱美。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Yongming he was envoy to Wei; the Wei envoy Li Biao announced the mandate and was greatly praised when he reached Yun.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Yongming he was envoy to Wei; Li Biao was greatly impressed when he reached Yun.

sentences.zh: 彪為設甘蔗、黃甘、粽，隨盡復益。

translations.literal: Biao set out sugarcane, sweet oranges, and rice dumplings; as soon as they were finished he replenished them.
translations.idiomatic: Biao set out sugarcane, sweet oranges, and dumplings; as soon as they were finished he replenished them.

sentences.zh: 彪笑謂曰：「範散騎小復儉之，一盡不可復得。」

translations.literal: Biao laughed and said, "Attendant Fan is a bit frugal again—once finished, no more can be had."
translations.idiomatic: Biao laughed, "Attendant Fan is frugal again—once finished, no more."

sentences.zh: 使還，再遷零陵內史。

translations.literal: On return from the mission he was twice promoted to Interior Minister of Lingling.
translations.idiomatic: On return he was twice promoted to interior minister of Lingling.

sentences.zh: 初，零陵舊政，公田奉米之外，別雜調四千石。

translations.literal: Earlier, the old policy of Lingling beyond the public-field rice tribute imposed an additional four thousand bushels in miscellaneous levies.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Lingling beyond public-field rice imposed four thousand bushels in miscellaneous levies.

sentences.zh: 及雲至郡，止其半，百姓悅之。

translations.literal: When Yun reached the commandery he stopped half of it and the people were pleased.
translations.idiomatic: When Yun arrived he stopped half and the people were pleased.

sentences.zh: 深為齊明帝所知，還除正員郎。

translations.literal: He was deeply known to Emperor Ming of Qi and on return was appointed Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming of Qi took note of him; on return he was appointed regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 時高、武王侯並懼大禍，雲因帝召次曰：「昔太宰文宣王語臣，言嘗夢在一高山上，上有一深坑，見文惠太子先墜，次武帝，次文宣。

translations.literal: At the time the princes of Gao and Wu all feared great disaster; when the Emperor summoned Yun he said in turn, "Formerly the late Grand Tutor Wenxuan Wang told me he once dreamed of being on a high mountain with a deep pit; he saw Crown Prince Wenhuizi fall first, then Emperor Wu, then Wenxuan.
translations.idiomatic: The princes of Gao and Wu feared disaster; Yun told the emperor, "Wenxuan Wang once dreamed of a high mountain and deep pit; Wenhuizi fell first, then Emperor Wu, then Wenxuan.

sentences.zh: 望見僕射在室坐御床，備王者羽儀，不知此是何夢，卿慎勿向人道。」

translations.literal: He saw the Vice Director seated in the chamber on the imperial couch with full royal regalia, not knowing what this dream meant—take care not to tell others."
translations.idiomatic: He saw the vice director on the imperial couch with full regalia—he did not know the dream's meaning and told me to tell no one."

sentences.zh: 明帝流涕曰：「文宣此惠亦難負。」

translations.literal: Emperor Ming wept and said, "Wenxuan's favor is also hard to repay."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming wept, "Wenxuan's favor is hard to repay."

sentences.zh: 於是處昭胄兄弟異于余宗室。

translations.literal: Thereupon he treated Zhaohou and his brothers differently from the rest of the imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: He treated Zhaohou and his brothers differently from the rest of the clan.

sentences.zh: 雲之幸於子良，江祏求雲女婚姻，酒酣，巾箱中取翦刀與雲，曰：「且以為娉。」

translations.literal: When Yun was favored by Ziliang, Jiang Shi sought marriage with Yun's daughter; when wine was deep he took scissors from his box and gave them to Yun, saying, "Let this serve as betrothal."
translations.idiomatic: When Yun was favored by Ziliang, Jiang Shi sought his daughter's hand; drunk, he gave Yun scissors as betrothal gift."

sentences.zh: 雲笑受之。

translations.literal: Yun smiled and accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Yun smiled and accepted.

sentences.zh: 至是祏貴，雲又因酣曰：「昔與將軍俱為黃鵠，今將軍化為鳳皇，荊布之室，理隔華盛。」

translations.literal: By then Shi was eminent; Yun again when drunk said, "Formerly we were both yellow swans; now you have become a phoenix—a house of coarse cloth is separated from splendor by reason."
translations.idiomatic: When Shi was eminent, Yun when drunk said, "We were both yellow swans; now you are a phoenix—a coarse house cannot match splendor."

sentences.zh: 因出翦刀還之，祏亦更姻他族。

translations.literal: He produced the scissors and returned them; Shi also betrothed his daughter elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: He returned the scissors; Shi betrothed his daughter elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 及祏敗，妻子流離，每相經理。

translations.literal: When Shi was defeated his wife and children were scattered; Yun always helped arrange matters for them.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi fell, his family was scattered; Yun always helped them.

sentences.zh: 又為始興內史，舊郡界得亡奴婢，悉付作；

translations.literal: He again served as Interior Minister of Shixing; in the old commandery recovered runaway slaves were all sent to corvée labor;
translations.idiomatic: He again served as interior minister of Shixing; recovered runaway slaves were sent to corvée;

sentences.zh: 部曲即貨去，買銀輸官。

translations.literal: retainers immediately sold them off and bought silver to deliver to the government.
translations.idiomatic: retainers sold them and bought silver for the government.

sentences.zh: 雲乃先聽百姓志之，若百日無主，依判送台。

translations.literal: Yun first allowed the common people to register them according to their wishes; if after a hundred days there was no owner, they were sent to the capital by judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Yun allowed people to register them; if after a hundred days there was no owner, they were sent to the capital.

sentences.zh: 又郡相承後堂有雜工作，雲悉省還役，並為帝所賞。

translations.literal: The commandery had also handed down miscellaneous labor in the rear hall; Yun abolished all and returned them to service, and the Emperor praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Miscellaneous labor in the rear hall was abolished and returned to service; the emperor praised him.

sentences.zh: 郡多豪猾大姓，二千石有不善者，輒共殺害，不則逐之。

translations.literal: The commandery had many powerful great clans; when a two-thousand-bushel official was unworthy they jointly killed him, or else drove him out.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery had many powerful clans; unworthy governors were killed or driven out.

sentences.zh: 邊帶蠻俚，尤多盜賊，前內史皆以兵刃自衛。

translations.literal: On the frontier with Man and Liao there were especially many bandits; previous interior ministers all guarded themselves with weapons.
translations.idiomatic: On the frontier with tribal peoples there were many bandits; previous ministers all carried weapons.

sentences.zh: 雲入境，撫以恩德，罷亭候，商賈露宿，郡中稱為神明。

translations.literal: When Yun entered the territory he soothed with kindness and virtue, abolished watch posts, and merchants slept in the open; the commandery called him divine.
translations.idiomatic: Yun soothed with kindness, abolished watch posts, and merchants slept in the open; the commandery called him divine.

sentences.zh: 遷廣州刺史、平越中郎將。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Governor of Guangzhou and General of the Pacification of Yue.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to governor of Guangzhou and general of the pacification of Yue.

sentences.zh: 至任，遣使祭孝子南海羅威唐頌、蒼梧丁密頓琦等墓。

translations.literal: On reaching his post he sent envoys to sacrifice at the tombs of the filial sons Luo Wei of Nanhai, Tang Song, Ding Mi, Dun Qi, and others.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching his post he sent envoys to sacrifice at tombs of filial sons Luo Wei, Tang Song, Ding Mi, Dun Qi, and others.

sentences.zh: 時江祏姨弟徐藝為曲江令，祏深以托云。

translations.literal: At the time Xu Yi, maternal cousin of Jiang Shi, was magistrate of Qujiang; Shi deeply entrusted him to Yun.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yi, Jiang Shi's maternal cousin, was magistrate of Qujiang; Shi entrusted him to Yun.

sentences.zh: 有譚儼者，縣之豪族，藝鞭之，儼以為恥，至都訴雲，雲坐征還下獄，會赦免。

translations.literal: There was Tan Yan, a powerful clan of the county; Yi flogged him and Yan, shamed, went to the capital to accuse Yun; Yun was recalled, imprisoned, and pardoned by amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Yan, a powerful clansman, was flogged by Yi; shamed, he accused Yun at court; Yun was recalled and imprisoned, then pardoned.

sentences.zh: 初，梁武為司徒祭酒，與雲俱在竟陵王西邸，情好歡甚。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Liang Wu was libationer of the Secretariat, he and Yun were both at the western residence of the Prince of Jingling and were very close.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Liang Wu and Yun were both at Jingling's western residence and were very close.

sentences.zh: 永明末，梁武與兄懿卜居東郊之外，雲亦築室相依。

translations.literal: At the end of Yongming Liang Wu and his brother Yi chose a residence outside the eastern suburbs; Yun also built a house nearby.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Yongming Liang Wu and Yi chose a residence outside the eastern suburbs; Yun built nearby.

sentences.zh: 梁武每至雲所，其妻常聞蹕聲。

translations.literal: Whenever Liang Wu came to Yun's place his wife often heard the sound of imperial escort.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang Wu visited, Yun's wife often heard imperial escort.

sentences.zh: 又嘗與梁武同宿顧暠之舍，暠之妻方產，有鬼在外曰：「此中有王有相。」

translations.literal: Once he stayed overnight at Gu Hao's house with Liang Wu; Hao's wife was giving birth and a ghost outside said, "Within are a king and a minister."
translations.idiomatic: Once he stayed with Liang Wu at Gu Hao's; Hao's wife was giving birth and a ghost said, "Within are a king and a minister."

sentences.zh: 雲起曰：「王當仰屬，相以見歸。」

translations.literal: Yun rose and said, "The king looks upward to belong; the minister is given in return."
translations.idiomatic: Yun said, "The king looks upward; the minister is given in return."

sentences.zh: 因是盡心推事。

translations.literal: From this he devoted himself wholeheartedly to serving him.
translations.idiomatic: From this he devoted himself to Liang Wu.

sentences.zh: 及帝起兵，將至都，雲雖無官，自以與帝素款，慮為昏主所疑，將求入城，先以車迎太原孫伯翳謀之。

translations.literal: When the Emperor raised arms and was about to reach the capital, though Yun had no office he thought himself long intimate with the Emperor and feared suspicion from the deluded ruler; wishing to enter the city he first sent his carriage to welcome Sun Boyi of Taiyuan to discuss.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang Wu marched on the capital, though without office Yun feared the deluded ruler's suspicion; wishing to enter the city he consulted Sun Boyi of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 伯翳曰：「今天文顯於上，災變應于下，蕭征東以濟世雄武，挾天子而令諸侯，天時人事，寧俟多說。」

translations.literal: Boyi said, "Today the astronomy is manifest above and disasters respond below; the eastern expedition pacifies the age with heroic martiality, holding the Son of Heaven to command the lords—Heaven, time, and men need no further words."
translations.idiomatic: Boyi said, "Heaven and earth show the signs; the eastern expedition holds the Son of Heaven to command the lords—no further words are needed."

sentences.zh: 雲曰：「此政會吾心，今羽翮未備，不得不就籠檻，希足下善聽之。」

translations.literal: Yun said, "This is just what is in my heart; now my wings are not ready and I must enter the cage—hope you will listen well."
translations.idiomatic: Yun said, "That is my heart; my wings are not ready and I must enter the cage—listen well."

sentences.zh: 及入城，除國子博士，未拜，而東昏遇弑。

translations.literal: When he entered the city he was appointed Erudite of the Imperial University but did not take office before Eastern Depravity was assassinated.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the city and was appointed erudite of the imperial university but did not take office before the emperor was assassinated.

sentences.zh: 侍中張稷使雲銜命至石頭，梁武恩待如舊，遂參贊謨謀，毗佐大業。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Zhang Ji had Yun carry the mandate to Stone City; Liang Wu treated him with favor as of old, and he then assisted in planning and aided the great enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ji had Yun carry the mandate to Stone City; Liang Wu treated him as before and he assisted the great enterprise.

sentences.zh: 仍拜黃門侍郎，與沈約同心翊贊。

translations.literal: He was then appointed Attendant of the Yellow Gate and, with Shen Yue, jointly supported the throne.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed attendant of the yellow gate and, with Shen Yue, jointly supported the throne.

sentences.zh: 俄遷大司馬諮議參軍，領錄事。

translations.literal: Before long he was promoted to Military Aide on the Staff of the Grand Marshal and concurrently Recorder.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was military aide on the grand marshal's staff and recorder.

sentences.zh: 梁台建，遷侍中。

translations.literal: When the Liang headquarters was established he was promoted to Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liang headquarters was established he became palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 武帝時納齊東昏餘妃，頗妨政事，雲嘗以為言，未之納。

translations.literal: The Emperor took a concubine left from Qi Eastern Depravity, which rather hindered government; Yun once spoke of it but it was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took a concubine of Eastern Depravity, which hindered government; Yun spoke but was not heeded.

sentences.zh: 後與王茂同入臥內，雲又諫，王茂因起拜曰：「範雲言是，公必以天下為念，無宜留惜。」

translations.literal: Later entering the sleeping quarters with Wang Mao, Yun remonstrated again; Wang Mao rose and bowed, saying, "Fan Yun is right—the public must think of the realm and should not be sparing."
translations.idiomatic: Entering with Wang Mao, Yun remonstrated again; Mao bowed and said, "Fan Yun is right—think of the realm, do not be sparing."

sentences.zh: 帝默然。

translations.literal: The Emperor was silent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was silent.

sentences.zh: 雲便疏令以餘氏賚茂，帝賢其意而許之。

translations.literal: Yun then memorialized to have the remainder given to Mao; the Emperor admired his intent and consented.
translations.idiomatic: Yun memorialized to give the woman to Mao; the emperor consented.

sentences.zh: 明日，賜雲、茂錢各百萬。

translations.literal: The next day he granted Yun and Mao a million cash each.
translations.idiomatic: Next day he granted Yun and Mao a million cash each.

sentences.zh: 及帝受禪，柴燎南郊，雲以侍中參乘。

translations.literal: When the Emperor received the abdication, at the southern suburb he burned firewood; Yun as Palace Attendant rode in the accompanying carriage.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor received the abdication, at the southern suburb Yun as palace attendant rode in the accompanying carriage.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，帝升輦謂雲曰：「朕之今日，所謂懍乎若朽索之馭六馬。」

translations.literal: When the rites were complete the Emperor mounted the carriage and said to Yun, "My present state is what is called trembling as if driving six horses with a rotten rope."
translations.idiomatic: When the rites ended the emperor said to Yun, "Today I tremble as if driving six horses with a rotten rope."

sentences.zh: 雲對曰：「亦願陛下日慎一日。」

translations.literal: Yun replied, "I also wish Your Majesty would be more cautious day by day."
translations.idiomatic: Yun replied, "I also wish Your Majesty would be more cautious day by day."

sentences.zh: 帝善其言，即日遷散騎常侍、吏部尚書。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved his words and that same day promoted him to Attendant Cavalier and Minister of the Civil Service.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved and that day made him attendant cavalier and minister of the civil service.

sentences.zh: 以佐命功，封霄城縣侯。

translations.literal: For merit in aiding the founding he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xiaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: For founding merit he was enfeoffed as marquis of Xiaocheng.

sentences.zh: 雲以舊恩，超居佐命，盡誠翊亮，知無不為。

translations.literal: Because of old favor Yun surpassed others in aiding the founding, devoted himself in support, and did all he knew.
translations.idiomatic: Because of old favor he surpassed others in aiding the founding and did all he knew.

sentences.zh: 帝亦推心仗之，所奏多允。

translations.literal: The Emperor also gave him his full trust; what he memorialized was mostly approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor gave him full trust; his memorials were mostly approved.

sentences.zh: 雲本大武帝十三歲，嘗侍宴，帝謂臨川王宏、鄱陽王恢曰：「我與范尚書少親善，申四海之敬。

translations.literal: Yun was originally thirteen years older than Emperor Wu; once when attending a feast the Emperor said to the Princes of Linchuan Hong and Poyang Hui, "I was close with Director Fan from youth and extended the respect due within the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: Yun was thirteen years older; at a feast the emperor told Princes Hong and Hui, "I was close with Director Fan from youth and extended the respect due within the four seas.

sentences.zh: 今為天下主，此禮既革，汝宜代我呼范為兄。」

translations.literal: Now I am lord of the realm and this ritual is changed—you should call Fan elder brother in my place."
translations.idiomatic: Now I am lord of the realm and this ritual is changed—you should call Fan elder brother for me."

sentences.zh: 二王下席拜，與雲同車還尚書下省，時人榮之。

translations.literal: The two princes left their seats and bowed; they returned with Yun in the same carriage to the vice director's office below the Secretariat, and people of the time regarded it as an honor.
translations.idiomatic: The princes bowed; they returned with Yun in the same carriage, and people regarded it as an honor.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗與雲言及舊事，云：「朕司州還，在三橋宅，門生王道牽衣雲，'聞外述圖讖雲，齊祚不久，別應有王者。

translations.literal: The Emperor once spoke with Yun of old matters, saying, "When I returned from the Directorate, at my house on the Third Bridge a student Wang Dao tugged my robe and said, 'I hear outsiders spreading charts and prophecies saying the Qi mandate will not last long and another king should arise.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor spoke of old matters: "At my house on the Third Bridge student Wang Dao tugged my robe and said outsiders spread prophecies that Qi would not last and another king should arise.

sentences.zh: 官應取富貴'。

translations.literal: Your office should take wealth and honor.
translations.idiomatic: Your office should take wealth and honor.

sentences.zh: 朕齋中坐讀書，內感其言而外跡不得無怪，欲呼人縛之，道叩頭求哀，乃不復敢言。

translations.literal: I was sitting in my study reading, inwardly moved by his words yet outwardly unable to show no surprise, and wished to have him bound; Dao kowtowed and begged for mercy and dared speak no more.
translations.idiomatic: I was reading in my study, inwardly moved yet outwardly surprised, and wished to bind him; Dao kowtowed and dared speak no more.

sentences.zh: 今道為羽林監、文德主帥，知管鑰。」

translations.literal: Now Dao is supervisor of the Feathered Forest and chief of the Wende gate, in charge of keys."
translations.idiomatic: Now Dao is supervisor of the feathered forest and chief of the Wende gate, in charge of keys."

sentences.zh: 雲曰：「此乃天意令道發耳。」

translations.literal: Yun said, "This was Heaven's will making Dao speak."
translations.idiomatic: Yun said, "This was Heaven's will making Dao speak."

sentences.zh: 帝又云：「布衣時，嘗夢拜兩舊妾為六宮，有天下，此嫗已卒，所拜非復其人，恒以為恨。」

translations.literal: The Emperor also said, "In commoner days I once dreamed of bowing to two old concubines as the Six Palaces; when I had the realm they were already dead and those I bowed to were no longer the persons— I always regret it."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also said, "As a commoner I dreamed of bowing to two old concubines as the Six Palaces; when I had the realm they were dead and those I bowed to were not they—I always regret it."

sentences.zh: 其年，雲以本官領太子中庶子。

translations.literal: That year Yun in his original office concurrently served as Junior Tutor of the Heir.
translations.idiomatic: That year Yun concurrently served as junior tutor of the heir.

sentences.zh: 二年，遷尚書右僕射，猶領吏部。

translations.literal: In the second year he was promoted to Right Vice Director of the Secretariat, still heading the Civil Service.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he became right vice director of the secretariat, still heading the civil service.

sentences.zh: 頃之，坐違詔用人，免吏部，猶為右僕射。

translations.literal: Before long, for violating an edict in appointments he was removed from the Civil Service but remained Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, for violating an edict in appointments he was removed from the civil service but remained right vice director.

sentences.zh: 雲性篤睦，事寡嫂盡禮，家事必先諮而後行。

translations.literal: Yun was by nature affectionate and harmonious, served his widowed sister-in-law with full ritual, and in household affairs always consulted before acting.
translations.idiomatic: Yun was affectionate and harmonious, served his widowed sister-in-law with full ritual, and always consulted before household affairs.

sentences.zh: 好節尚奇，專趨人之急。

translations.literal: He loved integrity and prized the extraordinary, and devoted himself to others' urgent needs.
translations.idiomatic: He prized integrity and the extraordinary and devoted himself to others' urgent needs.

sentences.zh: 少與領軍長史王畡善，雲起宅新成，移家始畢，畡亡於官舍，屍無所歸，雲以東廂給之。

translations.literal: In youth he was friendly with Chief Administrator Wang Xian of the Army; when Yun's new house was finished and he had just moved, Xian died in the official quarters with nowhere for the corpse; Yun gave him the east wing.
translations.idiomatic: He was friendly with chief administrator Wang Xian; when Yun's new house was finished Xian died with nowhere for the corpse; Yun gave him the east wing.

sentences.zh: 移屍自門入，躬自營唅，招復如禮，時人以為難。

translations.literal: The corpse was moved in through the gate; he personally arranged the mourning and summoned the soul according to ritual—people of the time thought it difficult.
translations.idiomatic: He moved the corpse in through the gate and personally arranged mourning—people thought it remarkable.

sentences.zh: 及居選官，任寄隆重，書牘盈案，賓客滿門，雲應答如流，無所壅滯，官曹文墨，發擿若神，時人咸服其明贍。

translations.literal: When he held office in appointments his trust was weighty; letters and documents filled the desk and guests filled the gate; Yun answered like flowing water without obstruction; official documents he dispatched as if by spirit—people of the time all admired his clarity.
translations.idiomatic: In appointments his trust was weighty; he answered like flowing water and dispatched documents as if by spirit—everyone admired his clarity.

sentences.zh: 性頗激厲，少威重，有所是非，形於造次，士或以此少之。

translations.literal: By nature he was rather impetuous with little imposing gravity; when he had an opinion he showed it at once, and gentlemen sometimes thought less of him for it.
translations.idiomatic: He was impetuous with little gravity; he showed opinions at once, and some thought less of him.

sentences.zh: 初，雲為郡號廉潔，及貴重，頗通饋遺；

translations.literal: Earlier when Yun was in commandery office he was called incorrupt; when he became eminent he rather accepted gifts;
translations.idiomatic: In commandery office he was called incorrupt; when eminent he accepted gifts;

sentences.zh: 然家無蓄積，隨散之親友。

translations.literal: yet the household had no stores and he gave away to kin and friends as he received.
translations.idiomatic: yet the household had no stores and he gave to kin and friends as he received.

sentences.zh: 武帝九錫之出，雲忽中疾，居二日半，召醫徐文伯視之。

translations.literal: When the Emperor's nine bestowments were issued Yun suddenly fell ill; after two and a half days the physician Xu Wenbo was summoned.
translations.idiomatic: When the nine bestowments were issued Yun suddenly fell ill; after two and a half days physician Xu Wenbo was summoned.

sentences.zh: 文伯曰：「緩之一月乃復，欲速即時愈，政恐二年不復可救。」

translations.literal: Wenbo said, "If treated slowly he will recover in a month; if you wish speed he will recover at once, but I fear in two years he will not be saveable."
translations.idiomatic: Wenbo said, "Slow treatment recovers in a month; speed recovers at once, but in two years he may not be saveable."

sentences.zh: 雲曰：「朝聞夕死，而況二年。」

translations.literal: Yun said, "To hear the Way at dawn and die at evening is enough—how much more two years."
translations.idiomatic: Yun said, "To hear the Way at dawn and die at evening is enough—how much more two years."

sentences.zh: 文伯乃下火而壯焉，重衣以覆之。

translations.literal: Wenbo then applied strong fire and covered him with heavy clothes.
translations.idiomatic: Wenbo applied strong fire and covered him with heavy clothes.

sentences.zh: 有頃，汗流於背即起。

translations.literal: Before long sweat streamed down his back and he rose at once.
translations.idiomatic: Soon sweat streamed down his back and he rose.

sentences.zh: 二年果卒。

translations.literal: In the second year he indeed died.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he indeed died.

sentences.zh: 帝為流涕，即日輿駕臨殯，詔贈侍中、衛將軍，禮官請諡曰宣，敕賜諡曰文。

translations.literal: The Emperor wept, that same day went in person to the lying-in-state, ordered posthumous appointment as Palace Attendant and Guard General; the ritual officers proposed the posthumous title Xuan, but an edict granted Wen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wept, went in person to the lying-in-state, ordered posthumous palace attendant and guard general; ritual officers proposed Xuan, but an edict granted Wen.

sentences.zh: 有集三十卷。

translations.literal: He left collected works in thirty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He left collected works in thirty scrolls.

sentences.zh: 子孝才嗣。

translations.literal: His son Xiaocai succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiaocai succeeded.

sentences.zh: 孫伯翳，太原人，晉秘書監盛之玄孫。

translations.literal: Sun Boyi was a man of Taiyuan, great-grandson of Jin Director of the Secretariat Sun Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Boyi was from Taiyuan, great-grandson of Jin director of the secretariat Sun Sheng.

sentences.zh: 曾祖放，晉國子博士、長沙太守。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Fang was Erudite of the Imperial University and Governor of Changsha in Jin.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Fang was erudite of the imperial university and governor of Changsha under Jin.

sentences.zh: 父康，起部郎，貧常映雪讀書，清介，交遊不雜。

translations.literal: His father Kang was a gentleman of the Ministry of Rites, poor and often reading by snowlight, pure and upright, with no mixed associations.
translations.idiomatic: His father Kang was a gentleman of the ministry of rites, poor, reading by snowlight, pure and upright.

sentences.zh: 伯翳位終驃騎鄱陽王參軍事。

translations.literal: Boyi ended as military aide to the Flying Cavalry General, Prince of Poyang.
translations.idiomatic: Boyi ended as military aide to the flying cavalry general, Prince of Poyang.

sentences.zh: 雲從父兄縝。

translations.literal: Yun's paternal cousin Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Yun's paternal cousin Zhen.

sentences.zh: 縝字子真。

translations.literal: Zhen, styled Zizhen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen, styled Zizhen.

sentences.zh: 父蒙，奉朝請，早卒。

translations.literal: His father Meng was a court gentleman and died young.
translations.idiomatic: His father Meng was a court gentleman and died young.

sentences.zh: 縝少孤貧，事母孝謹。

translations.literal: Zhen was orphaned and poor in youth and served his mother with filial care.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen was orphaned and poor and served his mother with filial care.

sentences.zh: 年未弱冠，從沛國劉瓛學，瓛甚奇之，親為之冠。

translations.literal: Before reaching the capping age he studied with Liu Huan of Pei; Huan greatly marveled at him and personally capped him.
translations.idiomatic: Before capping age he studied with Liu Huan of Pei; Huan marveled at him and personally capped him.

sentences.zh: 在瓛門下積年，恒芒屩布衣，徒行于路。

translations.literal: For many years in Huan's school he always wore straw sandals and plain cloth and walked on foot.
translations.idiomatic: For years in Huan's school he wore straw sandals and plain cloth and walked on foot.

sentences.zh: 瓛門下多車馬貴遊，縝在其間，聊無恥愧。

translations.literal: Huan's school had many noble students with carriages and horses; among them Zhen had not the slightest shame.
translations.idiomatic: Huan's school had many nobles with carriages; Zhen was not ashamed.

sentences.zh: 及長，博通經術，尤精三禮。

translations.literal: When grown he mastered the classics, especially the three Rites.
translations.idiomatic: When grown he mastered the classics, especially the three Rites.

sentences.zh: 性質直，好危言高論，不為士友所安。

translations.literal: By nature he was blunt and loved stern words and lofty discourse, which did not put scholar friends at ease.
translations.idiomatic: He was blunt and loved stern, lofty discourse, which unsettled scholar friends.

sentences.zh: 唯與外弟蕭琛善，琛名曰口辯，每服縝簡詣。

translations.literal: Only with his cousin on his mother's side Xiao Chen was he friendly; Chen was famed for eloquence and always yielded to Zhen's brevity.
translations.idiomatic: Only with cousin Xiao Chen was he friendly; Chen was famed for eloquence and yielded to Zhen's brevity.

sentences.zh: 年二十九，發白皤然，乃作傷暮詩、白髮詠以自嗟。

translations.literal: At twenty-nine his hair turned white; he wrote Lament for Declining Years and Song of White Hair to sigh over himself.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty-nine his hair turned white; he wrote Lament for Declining Years and Song of White Hair.

sentences.zh: 仕齊位尚書殿中郎。

translations.literal: In Qi he served as Palace Gentleman of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In Qi he served as palace gentleman of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 永明中，與魏氏和親，簡才學之士以為行人，縝及從弟雲、蕭琛、琅邪顏幼明、河東裴昭明相繼將命，皆著名鄰國。

translations.literal: In Yongming, when peace was made with Wei, talented scholars were chosen as envoys; Zhen and his cousin Yun, Xiao Chen, Yan Youming of Langye, and Pei Zhaoming of Hedong served as envoys in succession, all famed in neighboring states.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongming, for peace with Wei, talented envoys were chosen; Zhen, Yun, Chen, Yan Youming, and Pei Zhaoming served in succession, all famed abroad.

sentences.zh: 時竟陵王子良盛招賓客，縝亦預焉。

translations.literal: At the time the Prince of Jingling greatly gathered guests and Zhen also participated.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Jingling gathered guests and Zhen participated.

sentences.zh: 嘗侍子良，子良精信釋教，而縝盛稱無佛。

translations.literal: Once attending Ziliang, who deeply believed in Buddhism while Zhen strongly declared there was no Buddha.
translations.idiomatic: Once attending Ziliang, who believed in Buddhism while Zhen declared there was no Buddha.

sentences.zh: 子良問曰：「君不信因果，何得富貴貧賤？」

translations.literal: Ziliang asked, "If you do not believe in cause and effect, how do you get wealth and honor or poverty and lowliness?"
translations.idiomatic: Ziliang asked, "If you do not believe in cause and effect, how do wealth and poverty come?"

sentences.zh: 縝答曰：「人生如樹花同發，隨風而墮，自有拂簾幌墜于茵席之上，自有關籬牆落於糞溷之中。

translations.literal: Zhen answered, "Human life is like blossoms on a tree blooming together and falling with the wind—some brush the curtain and fall on cushions and mats;
translations.idiomatic: Zhen answered, "Life is like tree blossoms falling with the wind—some brush the curtain onto cushions;

sentences.zh: 墜茵席者，殿下是也；

translations.literal: some pass the fence and wall and fall into dung and mire.
translations.idiomatic: some pass the fence into dung and mire.

sentences.zh: 落糞溷者，下官是也。

translations.literal: Those who fall on cushions and mats—that is Your Highness;
translations.idiomatic: Those on cushions—that is Your Highness;

sentences.zh: 貴賤雖復殊途，因果竟在何處。」

translations.literal: those who fall into dung and mire—that is your servant.
translations.idiomatic: those in dung—that is your servant.

sentences.zh: 子良不能屈，然深怪之。

translations.literal: Wealth and poverty may have different paths, but where is cause and effect?"
translations.idiomatic: Wealth and poverty differ, but where is cause and effect?"

sentences.zh: 退論其理，著神滅論。

translations.literal: Ziliang could not refute him but was deeply struck by it.
translations.idiomatic: Ziliang could not refute him but was deeply struck.

sentences.zh: 以為：「神即形也，形即神也，形存則神存，形謝則神滅。

translations.literal: He held: "Soul is form and form is soul; when form exists the soul exists, when form perishes the soul is extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: He held: "Soul is form and form is soul; when form exists soul exists, when form perishes soul is extinguished.

sentences.zh: 形者神之質，神者形之用。

translations.literal: Form is the substance of the soul and the soul is the function of form.
translations.idiomatic: Form is the substance of soul and soul is the function of form.

sentences.zh: 是則形稱其質，神言其用，形之與神，不得相異。

translations.literal: Thus form names its substance and soul names its function; form and soul cannot differ.
translations.idiomatic: Thus form names substance and soul names function; form and soul cannot differ.

sentences.zh: 神之於質，猶利之於刀，形之於用，猶刀之於利。

translations.literal: Soul to substance is like sharpness to a knife; form to function is like a knife to sharpness.
translations.idiomatic: Soul to substance is like sharpness to a knife; form to function is like knife to sharpness.

sentences.zh: 利之名非刀也，刀之名非利也，然而舍利無刀，舍刀無利。

translations.literal: The name sharpness is not the knife and the name knife is not sharpness, yet apart from sharpness there is no knife and apart from the knife no sharpness.
translations.idiomatic: Sharpness is not the knife and knife is not sharpness, yet apart from sharpness there is no knife and apart from knife no sharpness.

sentences.zh: 未聞刀沒而利存，豈容形亡而神在。」

translations.literal: One never hears of the knife perishing while sharpness remains—how can form perish while the soul remains?"
translations.idiomatic: One never hears of the knife perishing while sharpness remains—how can form perish while soul remains?"

sentences.zh: 此論出，朝野喧嘩。

translations.literal: When this treatise appeared, court and commoners were in an uproar.
translations.idiomatic: When it appeared, court and commoners were in an uproar.

sentences.zh: 子良集僧難之而不能屈。

translations.literal: Ziliang gathered monks to challenge him but could not overcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Ziliang gathered monks to challenge him but could not overcome him.

sentences.zh: 太原王琰乃著論譏縝曰：「嗚呼範子！

translations.literal: Wang Yan of Taiyuan wrote a treatise mocking Zhen, saying, "Alas, Master Fan!
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan wrote a treatise mocking him: "Alas, Master Fan!

sentences.zh: 曾不知其先祖神靈所在。」

translations.literal: You do not know where your ancestors' spirits abide.
translations.idiomatic: You do not know where your ancestors' spirits abide.

sentences.zh: 欲杜縝後對。

translations.literal: He wished to cut off Zhen's replies.
translations.idiomatic: He wished to block Zhen's reply.

sentences.zh: 縝又對曰：「嗚呼王子！

translations.literal: Zhen replied again, "Alas, Master Wang!
translations.idiomatic: Zhen replied, "Alas, Master Wang!

sentences.zh: 知其祖先神靈所在，而不能殺身以從之。」

translations.literal: You know where your ancestors' spirits abide yet cannot kill yourself to follow them."
translations.idiomatic: You know where your ancestors' spirits abide yet cannot kill yourself to follow them."

sentences.zh: 其險詣皆此類也。

translations.literal: His sharp retorts were all of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: His sharp retorts were all of this sort.

sentences.zh: 子良使王融謂之曰：「神滅既自非理，而卿堅執之，恐傷名教。

translations.literal: Ziliang had Wang Rong tell him, "The extinction of the soul is itself against reason, and if you insist you will harm the teachings.
translations.idiomatic: Ziliang had Wang Rong tell him, "Soul extinction is against reason; if you insist you harm the teachings.

sentences.zh: 以卿之大美，何患不至中書郎，而故乖刺為此，可便毀棄之。」

translations.literal: With your great beauty, why fear not reaching Attendant of the Secretariat—yet you perversely make this; you should destroy it at once."
translations.idiomatic: With your great gifts, why fear not reaching attendant of the secretariat—destroy this at once."

sentences.zh: 縝大笑曰：「使範縝賣論取官，已至令僕矣，何但中書郎邪。」

translations.literal: Zhen laughed greatly and said, "If Fan Zhen sold treatises for office he would already be Vice Director—how much more Attendant of the Secretariat?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhen laughed, "If I sold treatises for office I would already be vice director—how much more attendant?"

sentences.zh: 後為宜都太守。

translations.literal: Later he was Governor of Yidu.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was governor of Yidu.

sentences.zh: 性不信神鬼，時夷陵有伍相廟、唐漢三神廟、胡裏神廟，縝乃下教斷不祠。

translations.literal: By nature he did not believe in ghosts and spirits; at the time Yiling had temples to Minister Wu, the Three Spirits of Tang and Han, and the Barbarian Li Spirit; Zhen issued orders forbidding sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: He did not believe in ghosts; at Yiling he forbade sacrifice at temples to Wu, the Three Spirits, and others.

sentences.zh: 後以母憂去職。

translations.literal: Later he left office for his mother's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Later he left office for mourning.

sentences.zh: 居於南州。

translations.literal: He dwelt in the southern province.
translations.idiomatic: He dwelt in the southern province.

sentences.zh: 梁武至，縝墨縗來迎。

translations.literal: When Liang Wu arrived, Zhen came in ink-stained mourning garb to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang Wu arrived, Zhen came in mourning garb to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 武帝與縝有西邸之舊，見之甚悅。

translations.literal: The Emperor and Zhen had old ties from the western residence and was greatly pleased to see him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor and Zhen had western residence ties and was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 及建康城平，以縝為晉安太守，在郡清約，資公祿而已。

translations.literal: When Jiankang was pacified Zhen was made Governor of Jin'an; in the commandery he was pure and frugal, living only on public salary.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiankang was pacified he was governor of Jin'an, pure and frugal, living only on salary.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書左丞，及還，雖親戚無所遺，唯餉前尚書令王亮。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Left Assistant Director of the Secretariat; on return, though he gave nothing to kin, he only presented gifts to former Director Wang Liang.
translations.idiomatic: He became left assistant director; on return he gave nothing to kin but presented gifts only to Wang Liang.

sentences.zh: 縝在齊時，與亮同台為郎，舊相友愛。

translations.literal: In Qi times he and Liang had been colleagues as gentlemen; they had been old friends.
translations.idiomatic: In Qi he and Liang had been colleagues and old friends.

sentences.zh: 至是亮擯棄在家，縝自以首迎武帝，志在權軸，而所懷未滿，亦怏怏，故私相親結，以矯于時。

translations.literal: Now Liang was cast aside at home; Zhen, because he had been first to welcome the Emperor and aspired to power, was not satisfied in his aims and therefore privately formed a bond to flatter the times.
translations.idiomatic: Now Liang was cast aside at home; Zhen, first to welcome the emperor yet unsatisfied in his aims, privately bonded with him to flatter the times.

sentences.zh: 竟坐亮徙廣州。

translations.literal: In the end because of Liang he was banished to Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the end because of Liang he was banished to Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 在南累年，追為中書郎，國子博士，卒。

translations.literal: In the south for many years he was recalled as Attendant of the Secretariat and Erudite of the Imperial University and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the south for years he was recalled as attendant of the secretariat and erudite of the imperial university and died.

sentences.zh: 文集十五卷。

translations.literal: Collected works in fifteen scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Collected works in fifteen scrolls.

sentences.zh: 子胥字長才，傳父業，位國子博士，有口辯。

translations.literal: His son Xu, styled Changcai, inherited his father's work, served as Erudite of the Imperial University, and was famed for eloquence.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xu, styled Changcai, inherited his father's work, served as erudite of the imperial university, and was famed for eloquence.

sentences.zh: 大同中，常兼主客郎，應接北使，卒于鄱陽內史。

translations.literal: In Datong he often concurrently served as chief guest officer receiving northern envoys and died as Interior Minister of Poyang.
translations.idiomatic: In Datong he often received northern envoys as chief guest officer and died as interior minister of Poyang.

sentences.zh: 論曰：齊德將謝，昏虐君臨，喋喋黔黎，命懸晷刻。

translations.literal: Discussion: When Qi virtue was about to decline, a deluded and cruel ruler held the throne; the chattering common people hung by the moment.
translations.idiomatic: Discussion: When Qi virtue declined, a cruel ruler held the throne and the people hung by the moment.

sentences.zh: 梁武撫茲歸運，嘯召風雲。

translations.literal: Liang Wu took hold of this returning fortune and whistled to summon the wind and clouds.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Wu took hold of returning fortune and summoned wind and clouds.

sentences.zh: 范雲恩結龍潛，沈約情深惟舊，並以茲文義，首居帷幄，追蹤亂傑，各其時之遇也。

translations.literal: Fan Yun's grace bound him while hidden like a dragon; Shen Yue's feeling was deep with old ties; both by this literary righteousness first occupied the inner counsel, following the heroes of disorder—each met the fortune of his time.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Yun bound him while hidden; Shen Yue's feeling was deep with old ties; both by literary righteousness first occupied inner counsel—each met his time.

sentences.zh: 而約以高才博洽，名亞董、遷，末跡為躓，亦鳳德之衰乎。

translations.literal: Yet Yue, with lofty talent and broad learning, ranked in name below Dong and Qian; his final stumble was also the decline of phoenix virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Yue, with lofty talent, ranked below Dong and Qian; his final stumble was decline of phoenix virtue.

sentences.zh: 縝婞直之節，著於終始，其以王亮為尤，亦不足非也。

translations.literal: Zhen's upright integrity was manifest from beginning to end; that he made Wang Liang his chief fault is also not to be blamed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen's upright integrity was manifest throughout; that he made Wang Liang his chief fault is also not to be blamed.
